# Alchemy

> Alchemy Effect is an Infrastructure-as-Effects (IaE) framework that combines cloud infrastructure and application logic into a single, type-safe program powered by [Effect](https://effect.website). Resources are declared as Effects; bindings wire IAM, env vars, and typed SDKs in one call; deploys and runtime share the same code.

This file is a navigation index for the documentation site at https://alchemy.run. Guide and concept pages are listed below with their URL and a one-line summary, so an agent can pick the right page in one hop. The service-level API reference is indexed separately in [llms-full.txt](https://alchemy.run/llms-full.txt).

## Start here

- [What is Alchemy?](https://alchemy.run/what-is-alchemy) — Alchemy is a TypeScript framework for building cloud applications with Effects and Layers. Your infrastructure and the code that runs on it are written, type-checked, and deployed together.
- [Getting started](https://alchemy.run/getting-started) — Install Alchemy and create your first Stack in under two minutes.
- [Migrating from v1](https://alchemy.run/migrating-from-v1) — Migrate your Alchemy v1 (async/await) project to Alchemy v2.

## CLI

Every command runs through your package manager: bun alchemy <command>. Command pages by role, the Programmatic API for running them from scripts, plus the Adopting Resources and Inspecting State guides.

- [CLI](https://alchemy.run/cli) — Every alchemy command at a glance — the command map, common options, and how the interactive TUI decides when to render.
- [Programmatic API](https://alchemy.run/cli/api) — Run deploy, plan, destroy, drift, nuke, logs, and state from your own scripts with alchemy/Alchemist.
- [deploy](https://alchemy.run/cli/deploy) — Compute a plan, ask for approval, and create/update/delete resources to match the desired state.
- [plan](https://alchemy.run/cli/plan) — Preview what would change without applying anything. Equivalent to alchemy deploy --dry-run.
- [destroy](https://alchemy.run/cli/destroy) — Delete every resource in a stack — plan all existing resources for deletion, ask for approval, and remove them in dependency order.
- [drift](https://alchemy.run/cli/drift) — Detect infrastructure drift by re-observing the cloud, and optionally repair it back to the last deployed state.
- [nuke](https://alchemy.run/cli/nuke) — Enumerate and delete every live resource across the stack's providers.
- [Adopting Resources](https://alchemy.run/cli/adopting-resources) — How alchemy takes ownership of pre-existing cloud resources — recovery by default, --adopt for foreign resources, and the programmatic AdoptPolicy.
- [dev](https://alchemy.run/cli/dev) — Run your stack in development mode with hot reloading — resources deploy to the cloud while Workers run in the local dev runtime.
- [logs](https://alchemy.run/cli/logs) — Fetch or tail logs from deployed resources, merged and color-coded by resource.
- [profile](https://alchemy.run/cli/profile) — Create, refresh, rename, edit, inspect, or delete Alchemy authentication profiles.
- [state](https://alchemy.run/cli/state) — Browse, read, and delete entries in the state store.
- [Inspecting State](https://alchemy.run/cli/inspecting-state) — See what alchemy thinks is deployed, debug a bad diff, and recover from bad state.
- [aws](https://alchemy.run/cli/aws) — AWS provider commands — bootstrap the per-account assets bucket that Lambda deployments rely on.
- [cloudflare](https://alchemy.run/cli/cloudflare) — Cloudflare provider commands — mint API tokens.

## Infrastructure as Code

The noun graph and its semantics: Stacks of Resources and Actions, data flow via Inputs & Outputs and References, deploy behavior via the Resource lifecycle and Providers.

- [Stacks](https://alchemy.run/infrastructure-as-code/stack) — A Stack is a collection of Resources deployed together as a unit.
- [Resources](https://alchemy.run/infrastructure-as-code/resource) — Resources are named cloud entities with input properties and output attributes.
- [Actions](https://alchemy.run/infrastructure-as-code/action) — A node in the dependency graph that runs an Effect during apply when its inputs change.
- [Inputs & Outputs](https://alchemy.run/infrastructure-as-code/outputs) — Output<T> is alchemy's lazy reference type — the lazy values that flow between resources, get composed with .pipe, mapped, interpolated, and resolved during deploy.
- [References](https://alchemy.run/infrastructure-as-code/references) — Read an already-deployed Resource or Stack at plan time — Resource.ref by Logical ID with optional stack/stage props, Resource.lookup for resources Alchemy doesn't manage, or import a Stack tag and depend on its outputs.
- [Resource Lifecycle](https://alchemy.run/infrastructure-as-code/resource-lifecycle) — How alchemy plans, applies, replaces, and destroys resources — and how to think about idempotency and recovery.
- [Renaming Resources](https://alchemy.run/infrastructure-as-code/renaming) — Migrate a resource's state across a logical ID change instead of replacing it.
- [Providers](https://alchemy.run/infrastructure-as-code/provider) — Providers implement the lifecycle operations for a resource type — reconcile, delete, diff, read, and more.
- [Custom Provider](https://alchemy.run/infrastructure-as-code/custom-provider) — Add support for a new cloud or third-party API by declaring a Resource type and implementing its lifecycle as an Effect Layer.
- [Local Provider](https://alchemy.run/infrastructure-as-code/local-provider) — Build the local implementation of a resource — dual registration with ProviderLayer.dual and the LocalProvider runner for long-running processes.
- [DNS Adapters](https://alchemy.run/infrastructure-as-code/dns-adapters) — Publish a custom domain's DNS records in Route 53, Cloudflare, or Hetzner DNS from any platform, and build an adapter for another DNS host.
- [Provider Contributions](https://alchemy.run/infrastructure-as-code/contributions) — Ship a provider's auth, state stores and CLI commands in a package, so the alchemy CLI finds them without a stack.

## Infrastructure as Effects

How app code and infrastructure compose: Runtime, Bindings, the Construction and Runtime Phases, and Layers.

- [Runtime](https://alchemy.run/infrastructure-as-effects/runtime) — A Runtime is a Resource that carries the code it runs — a Worker, Lambda Function, Container, or Server declared with the Effectful Constructor pattern. Bind what you need, return what you expose.
- [Bindings](https://alchemy.run/infrastructure-as-effects/binding) — A Binding connects a Resource to a Worker or Lambda. One line declares the capability and generates the permissions, the configuration, and a typed client.
- [Identity Federation](https://alchemy.run/infrastructure-as-effects/identity-federation) — How a binding reaches another cloud with the identity the host's platform already signs, instead of a long-lived key, and which runtimes and clouds support it.
- [Layers](https://alchemy.run/infrastructure-as-effects/layers) — A Layer defines a service contract with swappable implementations. In Alchemy, a Layer can encapsulate Resources and Bindings, so shared services carry their own infrastructure and permissions.
- [Event Sources](https://alchemy.run/infrastructure-as-effects/event-sources) — An event source is a binding that runs your Function when something happens on a resource — one call wires the event-source mapping, the permissions, and a typed handler.
- [Sinks](https://alchemy.run/infrastructure-as-effects/sinks) — A Sink is the write-side dual of an Event Source — a Binding that exposes a resource as an Effect Sink, batching writes into the batch API with least-privilege IAM.
- [Phases](https://alchemy.run/infrastructure-as-effects/phases) — Alchemy programs run in two phases — Construction drives the deploy, Runtime handles requests. Knowing which is which is the key to writing Workers and Lambda Functions.
- [Circular Bindings](https://alchemy.run/infrastructure-as-effects/circular-bindings) — How to model two services that reference each other (Worker A ↔ Worker B, Lambda ↔ Lambda) using tagged classes and Layers.
- [Custom Runtime](https://alchemy.run/infrastructure-as-effects/custom-runtime) — Implement your own Runtime resource on the Platform type — a Provider that provisions the compute and bundles the runtime Effect.
- [Telemetry](https://alchemy.run/infrastructure-as-effects/telemetry) — OpenTelemetry is built into every runtime — exporters are Layers, wired to resources through the binding infrastructure, built per event, and flushed as each request completes.

## APIs

Typed calls between Functions and Servers: schemaless RPC for internal communication, Effect RPC and Effect HTTP for trust boundaries.

- [APIs](https://alchemy.run/apis) — Every Function and Server returns { fetch, ...rpcs } — schemaless typed calls are the default for internal communication; Effect RPC and Effect HTTP add schemas where data crosses a trust boundary.
- [Schemaless RPC](https://alchemy.run/apis/schemaless) — The pattern behind typed, schema-free RPC — what an RPC member may be, how the typed client arises, how calls travel over the wire, and where the limits are.
- [Effect RPC](https://alchemy.run/apis/effect-rpc) — Schema-first RPC for trust boundaries — declare procedures, construct handler Layers, derive typed clients from the same schema.
- [Effect HTTP](https://alchemy.run/apis/effect-http) — Schema-validated REST endpoints with an rpc-like typed interface — for trust boundaries where consumers want a plain HTTP client.

## Environments — the same app in many places

Stages, credential profiles, auth providers, secrets and config, local development, and CI.

- [Stages](https://alchemy.run/environments/stages) — Stages are isolated instances of a Stack — live_sam, dev_sam, staging, prod, pr-42 — each with their own state and physical names.
- [Profiles](https://alchemy.run/environments/profiles) — Use profiles to select cloud accounts and credentials for each environment.
- [Auth Providers](https://alchemy.run/environments/auth-providers) — An Auth Provider produces the credentials for a cloud's API calls — resolved lazily as Effects, so tokens and role sessions can refresh instead of pinning one static key.
- [Custom Auth Provider](https://alchemy.run/environments/custom-auth-provider) — Add profile and CI credentials for a third-party API with a generated AuthProvider.
- [Secrets & Config](https://alchemy.run/environments/secrets) — Use effect/Config to read env vars at Construction time and have Alchemy automatically bind them onto the deploy target.
- [Secret providers](https://alchemy.run/environments/secret-providers) — Configure a stack with dotenv files, environment variables, Doppler, or Infisical.
- [Doppler](https://alchemy.run/environments/doppler) — Load a Doppler config into your Stack — log in with the browser on your machine, use a service token in CI.
- [Infisical](https://alchemy.run/environments/infisical) — Load an Infisical environment into your Stack — a machine identity on your machine, the platform's own OIDC token in CI.
- [Local development](https://alchemy.run/environments/local-development) — How alchemy dev provides hot reloading, local execution, and local emulation with per-resource opt-in to real cloud services.
- [Worktrees](https://alchemy.run/environments/worktrees) — Run alchemy deploy, dev, and tests from several git worktrees at once — one stage per worktree, so parallel agents never touch each other's resources.
- [CI](https://alchemy.run/environments/ci) — Set up CI/CD pipelines for alchemy projects with GitHub Actions, automated deployments, and PR previews — with provider credentials managed as code.

## State Store

- [State Store](https://alchemy.run/state-store) — How Alchemy persists resource state between deploys to compute diffs and track infrastructure.
- [Custom State Store](https://alchemy.run/state-store/custom-state-store) — Build a Postgres-backed Alchemy state store step by step — implement the StateService interface, plug it into a stack, and test it end-to-end.

## Project structure

Scaling the codebase: file conventions for one stack, monorepos for many — single Stack or one per package.

- [File layout](https://alchemy.run/project-structure/file-layout) — How to organize an Alchemy project — one file per Resource or Layer, group Resources that travel together by concern, and keep alchemy.run.ts as the composition root.
- [Monorepo](https://alchemy.run/project-structure/monorepo) — Two ways to organize an Alchemy monorepo — one Stack at the workspace root, or one Stack per package wired with typed references.
- [Single Stack](https://alchemy.run/project-structure/monorepo-single-stack) — One alchemy.run.ts at the workspace root deploys every app in the monorepo — one plan, one state file, and every path anchored to the file that declares it.
- [Multiple Stacks](https://alchemy.run/project-structure/monorepo-multi-stack) — Each package owns its own alchemy.run.ts. The frontend consumes the backend's deployed outputs through a typed Stack handle, resolved from the state store at plan time, so each package deploys and destroys independently.

## Testing & observability

Tests run against real clouds: the model, the end-to-end walkthrough, provider-lifecycle testing, and the harness reference.

- [Testing](https://alchemy.run/testing) — How Alchemy tests work — real clouds by default, local emulators on demand, one Stack deploy per suite, isolated stages, deploy → assert → destroy.
- [Testing a Stack](https://alchemy.run/testing/testing-a-stack) — Deploy your real Stack once per suite, drive it over HTTP, tear it down.
- [Testing Providers](https://alchemy.run/testing/testing-providers) — Exercise a provider's create, update, replace, and delete paths with test.provider and a scratch in-memory stack.
- [Test harness](https://alchemy.run/testing/test-harness) — Reference for @alchemy.run/test — every helper, hook, and option exposed by Test.make, and how to run it with alchemy-test, bun test, or Vitest.
- [Observability](https://alchemy.run/testing/observability) — Effect emits OpenTelemetry natively and the exporter is a Layer. Provision the receiving end — datasets, monitors, notifiers, alarms — as resources in the same Stack as the code that emits the signals.

## Cloudflare — start here

The Cloudflare hub: overview, What is Cloudflare? (accounts, zones, Workers, bindings, Durable Objects, storage, queues, workflows, containers, API tokens and how Alchemy models each), setup (install, account, OAuth vs API token, profiles), and local development.

- [Cloudflare](https://alchemy.run/cloudflare) — Build on Cloudflare with Alchemy. Declare Workers, Durable Objects, R2, D1, KV and Queues in TypeScript, and bind each one into the Worker that uses it with a typed client.
- [What is Cloudflare?](https://alchemy.run/cloudflare/what-is-cloudflare) — The concepts behind Cloudflare — accounts, zones, the global network, Workers, bindings, Durable Objects, storage, queues, workflows, containers and API tokens — and how @alchemy.run/cloudflare models each of them.
- [Accounts and API tokens](https://alchemy.run/cloudflare/accounts-and-tokens) — How a Cloudflare account holds your Workers, storage and zones, how Alchemy signs in to it with OAuth or an API token, and how your Stack mints scoped tokens for CI and runtimes.
- [Setup](https://alchemy.run/cloudflare/setup) — Install Alchemy, create a Cloudflare account, and connect the two — OAuth or API token, saved to a local profile. No environment variables required.
- [Local development](https://alchemy.run/cloudflare/local-development) — alchemy dev runs Workers in workerd with local simulators for KV, R2, D1, Queues, Hyperdrive, Workflows, Containers, and the Worker binding surface — browser rendering, images, email, cron, Stream, and more.

## Cloudflare — tutorial

A linear six-part walkthrough from zero to a tested, locally-developed, CI-deployed, observable Cloudflare project. Each part builds on the previous one.

- [Part 1: Your First Stack](https://alchemy.run/cloudflare/tutorial/part-1) — Install Alchemy, create a Stack with a Cloudflare R2 Bucket, and deploy it.
- [Part 2: Add a Worker](https://alchemy.run/cloudflare/tutorial/part-2) — Create a Cloudflare Worker, bind the R2 Bucket, and implement GET/PUT routes.
- [Part 3: Testing](https://alchemy.run/cloudflare/tutorial/part-3) — Write integration tests that deploy your stack and make HTTP requests against your live Worker.
- [Part 4: Local Dev](https://alchemy.run/cloudflare/tutorial/part-4) — Run your stack locally with alchemy dev for hot reloading and instant feedback.
- [Part 5: CI/CD](https://alchemy.run/cloudflare/tutorial/part-5) — Set up GitHub Actions for automated deployments, PR previews, and remote state — with Cloudflare credentials managed as code.
- [Part 6: Observability](https://alchemy.run/cloudflare/tutorial/part-6) — Ship your Worker traces and logs to Axiom — datasets, an ingest token, and the Axiom.Telemetry binding layer declared in the same Stack as the Worker they observe.

## Cloudflare — Compute

- [Worker Previews](https://alchemy.run/cloudflare/compute/previews) — Deploy a branch or pull request as a first-class Preview of another Worker — its own URL, bindings, and isolated Durable Object state, without touching production traffic.
- [Accept WebSockets](https://alchemy.run/cloudflare/compute/hibernatable-websockets) — Accept WebSocket connections in a Durable Object, broadcast between peers, and survive Cloudflare's hibernation.
- [Bind to another Worker's Durable Object](https://alchemy.run/cloudflare/compute/cross-worker-durable-object) — Share a Durable Object across multiple Workers — one Worker hosts the runtime, others bind to it by scriptName for a typed RPC stub — and move the host later with the data intact.
- [Add a Workflow](https://alchemy.run/cloudflare/compute/add-a-workflow) — Orchestrate durable, multi-step work with Cloudflare Workflows — automatic retries, replayable steps, and at-least-once delivery.
- [Run a Container](https://alchemy.run/cloudflare/compute/run-a-container) — Run a long-lived container alongside a Durable Object, expose RPC methods, and proxy HTTP requests to ports inside the container.
- [Rate limiting](https://alchemy.run/cloudflare/compute/rate-limiting) — Throttle requests inside a Worker with Cloudflare's Rate Limiting binding — declare the limit on the binding, count arbitrary keys at runtime, handle failures as typed errors.
- [Workers Cache](https://alchemy.run/cloudflare/compute/cache) — Serve responses from Cloudflare's edge cache before your Worker even runs — enable it with one yield, control it with standard headers, purge it by tag from inside a handler.
- [Browser rendering](https://alchemy.run/cloudflare/compute/browser-rendering) — Attach Cloudflare Browser Rendering to a Worker — run quick actions like markdown and scrape, stream screenshots and PDFs, or drive the raw binding with puppeteer.
- [Worker Loader](https://alchemy.run/cloudflare/compute/worker-loader) — Load and run ephemeral Workers at runtime from inline source — each in its own sandboxed isolate, with optional outbound-network control and typed RPC entrypoints.
- [Workers for Platforms](https://alchemy.run/cloudflare/compute/workers-for-platforms) — Run your customers' Workers in your own account — create a dispatch namespace, upload user Workers into it, and route requests from a platform Worker with the Get binding.
- [Code updates](https://alchemy.run/cloudflare/compute/code-updates) — What happens to running Workers and Durable Objects when you deploy, how to choose when Durable Objects pick up new code, and how to write tests that see the code you just deployed.
- [Container lifecycle](https://alchemy.run/cloudflare/compute/container-lifecycle) — Start, stop, wait for, and restore a Cloudflare Container from its Durable Object — and save its filesystem as a snapshot to restore later.
- [Containers](https://alchemy.run/cloudflare/compute/containers) — Cloudflare Containers run long-lived processes beside a Durable Object — declare a typed container class, implement its runtime in a separate file, and alchemy builds the image, pushes it, and wires the DO pairing.
- [Durable Objects](https://alchemy.run/cloudflare/compute/durable-objects) — Durable Objects are globally-unique stateful instances with transactional storage — define one as an Effect, persist state per key, expose typed RPC methods, and stream values back to the caller.
- [Effect workflows](https://alchemy.run/cloudflare/compute/effect-workflows) — Run Effect workflows on Cloudflare, on Durable Objects or Cloudflare Workflows. Declare a workflow with effect/workflow, implement it with Workflows.layer, start runs with Workflows.RunWorkflow, and let them sleep, wait for signals and undo steps durably.
- [Gradual deployments](https://alchemy.run/cloudflare/compute/gradual-deployments) — Roll out Worker deploys incrementally — upload preview versions, canary a percentage of live traffic, ramp to 100%, pin users to a version during the rollout, and verify which version served each request.
- [Python Workers](https://alchemy.run/cloudflare/compute/python-workers) — Deploy Cloudflare Python Workers by pointing main at a .py file — alchemy uploads the modules, vendors pyproject.toml dependencies with uv, and serves them locally through workerd's built-in Pyodide.
- [Workers](https://alchemy.run/cloudflare/compute/workers) — Cloudflare Workers are the compute Runtime of every Alchemy app — declare the Worker and its handler in one file, bind resources with full type safety, and call other Workers over schemaless RPC.
- [Workflows](https://alchemy.run/cloudflare/compute/workflows) — Cloudflare Workflows run durable multi-step jobs — define a typed workflow class, checkpoint steps with task and sleep, trigger instances from a Worker, and poll status until completion.

## Cloudflare — Frontend

- [Frontend frameworks](https://alchemy.run/cloudflare/frontend/frontends) — Deploy Vite, Foldkit, Astro, Next.js, vinext, Nuxt, SvelteKit, Waku, or any static build to Cloudflare Workers with first-class Website resources.
- [Vite](https://alchemy.run/cloudflare/frontend/vite) — Deploy any pure-Vite app to Cloudflare Workers with a single resource.
- [Static sites](https://alchemy.run/cloudflare/frontend/static-site) — Deploy any build command's output directory as Cloudflare Worker static assets with Cloudflare.Website.StaticSite — custom edge Workers, framework-native local dev, and memoized rebuilds.
- [Add a React SPA](https://alchemy.run/cloudflare/frontend/vite-spa) — Ship a React single-page app from the same Stack as your Worker — built with Vite and deployed to Cloudflare in one command.
- [TanStack Start](https://alchemy.run/cloudflare/frontend/tanstack-start) — Deploy TanStack Start (React or Solid) to Cloudflare with Cloudflare.Website.Vite — SSR, typed Worker bindings, and HMR dev with real cloud resources.
- [Full-stack TanStack Start + RPC + Drizzle](https://alchemy.run/cloudflare/frontend/full-stack-tanstack-rpc-drizzle) — Build a reactive full-stack app on Cloudflare — a TanStack Start UI that drives an Effect RPC backend over Drizzle and Neon Postgres, with browser state wired through Effect 4's native atom RPC.
- [React Router](https://alchemy.run/cloudflare/frontend/react-router) — Deploy React Router v8 — including React Server Components — to Cloudflare with Cloudflare.Website.Vite and viteEnvironments.
- [Vue](https://alchemy.run/cloudflare/frontend/vue) — Deploy a Vue single-page app to Cloudflare with the Vite resource — one declaration, no Wrangler config.
- [Foldkit](https://alchemy.run/cloudflare/frontend/foldkit) — Deploy Foldkit SPA, SSR, SSG, and hybrid applications to Cloudflare Workers.
- [SolidStart](https://alchemy.run/cloudflare/frontend/solidstart) — Deploy SolidStart to Cloudflare with Cloudflare.Website.Vite — plus the hand-rolled SolidJS SSR variant for full control over the server entry.
- [Astro](https://alchemy.run/cloudflare/frontend/astro) — Deploy an Astro site to Cloudflare Workers with Cloudflare.Website.Astro — SSR in the Worker, prerendered pages as static assets, sessions backed by an auto-provisioned KV namespace, and route caching on Workers Cache.
- [Next.js](https://alchemy.run/cloudflare/frontend/nextjs) — Deploy a Next.js app to Cloudflare Workers with Cloudflare.Website.Nextjs — the OpenNext pipeline, writable ISR, and wrangler-free local dev.
- [Vinext](https://alchemy.run/cloudflare/frontend/vinext) — Deploy vinext to Cloudflare Workers with the shared Website API, native local development, and KV-backed caching.
- [Nuxt](https://alchemy.run/cloudflare/frontend/nuxt) — Deploy a Nuxt app to Cloudflare Workers with Cloudflare.Website.Nuxt — nitro's cloudflare_module preset, native nuxt.config.ts loading, and wrangler-free local dev.
- [SvelteKit](https://alchemy.run/cloudflare/frontend/sveltekit) — Deploy a SvelteKit app to Cloudflare Workers with Cloudflare.Website.SvelteKit — a wrangler-free in-memory adapter, real bindings on platform.env, and full-HMR local dev.
- [Waku](https://alchemy.run/cloudflare/frontend/waku) — Deploy a Waku app to Cloudflare Workers with Cloudflare.Website.Waku — RSC server in the Worker, SSG pages as static assets, and a custom-entry seam for Durable Objects.
- [Octane](https://alchemy.run/cloudflare/frontend/octane) — Deploy an OctaneJS fullstack app to Cloudflare Workers with Cloudflare.Website.Octane — native Octane and Vite configuration, no hosting adapter or Wrangler file required.

## Cloudflare — APIs

- [Schemaless RPC](https://alchemy.run/cloudflare/apis/schemaless-rpc) — Typed RPC between Workers, Durable Objects, and Containers with no schema — bind the class, get the client.
- [Effect HTTP API](https://alchemy.run/cloudflare/apis/effect-http-api) — Build a schema-validated HTTP API with Effect's HttpApi module and deploy it as a Cloudflare Worker.
- [Effect RPC](https://alchemy.run/cloudflare/apis/effect-rpc) — Build a typed RPC API with Effect's Rpc module and deploy it as a Cloudflare Worker.

## Cloudflare — Data

- [Store Git Repos with Artifacts](https://alchemy.run/cloudflare/data/artifacts) — Use Cloudflare Artifacts to create Git repos at runtime and hand out clone tokens, all from a tiny Worker.
- [Add Drizzle ORM](https://alchemy.run/cloudflare/data/drizzle) — Deploy a Cloudflare Worker with Drizzle queries, Hyperdrive connections, and reviewed, committed migrations on Neon or PlanetScale.
- [Branch from a shared database](https://alchemy.run/cloudflare/data/branch-from-shared-database) — Have ephemeral PR-preview stages reference a long-lived Neon or PlanetScale database from a staging stage instead of provisioning their own — fast previews, cheap branches, no extra clusters.
- [D1](https://alchemy.run/cloudflare/data/d1) — How D1 runs a SQLite database for your app, where its primary and read replicas live, how migrations are applied on deploy, and how Workers query it through a binding or Effect SQL.
- [Drizzle on D1](https://alchemy.run/cloudflare/data/d1-drizzle) — Deploy committed SQLite migrations to D1 and query the database from a Worker with Drizzle.
- [Hyperdrive](https://alchemy.run/cloudflare/data/hyperdrive) — Cloudflare Hyperdrive pools connections to your external Postgres or MySQL database at the edge — provision a database (Neon or PlanetScale), front it with Hyperdrive, and bind the connection into your Worker.
- [Iceberg tables](https://alchemy.run/cloudflare/data/iceberg-tables) — Turn an R2 bucket into an Apache Iceberg warehouse with Cloudflare's catalog, manage tables with schema evolution and maintenance, and query them from Spark, DuckDB, or PyIceberg.
- [KV](https://alchemy.run/cloudflare/data/kv) — How Workers KV replicates values to every city for fast reads, what eventual consistency means for writes, and how Workers read, write, list and expire keys through access-scoped bindings.
- [Pipelines](https://alchemy.run/cloudflare/data/pipelines) — Ingest events into R2 with Cloudflare Pipelines — a typed stream, a SQL pipeline, and a sink that writes JSON or Parquet files, or Apache Iceberg tables.
- [Prisma ORM with Postgres](https://alchemy.run/cloudflare/data/prisma) — Deploy Prisma ORM v8 on Cloudflare Workers with Neon Postgres, Hyperdrive, controlled migrations, and Effect-native queries.
- [Private database (Workers VPC)](https://alchemy.run/cloudflare/data/hyperdrive-private-database) — Connect Hyperdrive to a database inside a private network — such as Aurora in an AWS VPC — through a Cloudflare Tunnel and a Workers VPC Service, with no public endpoint.
- [R2](https://alchemy.run/cloudflare/data/r2) — How R2 Buckets store objects under keys with no egress fees, how Workers read and write them through access-scoped bindings, and how to share, serve, expire and delete what you store.
- [R2 presigned URLs](https://alchemy.run/cloudflare/data/r2-presigned-urls) — Mint presigned R2 URLs so browsers upload and download objects directly, with the same code in alchemy dev and in production, from Effect-native or async Workers.
- [Shared database across stages](https://alchemy.run/cloudflare/data/shared-database) — Have ephemeral PR-preview stages reference a long-lived Neon or PlanetScale database from a staging stage instead of provisioning their own — fast previews, copy-on-write branches, no extra clusters.

## Cloudflare — Messaging & events

- [Scheduled jobs with Cron Triggers](https://alchemy.run/cloudflare/messaging/cron) — Run Worker code on a schedule — declare a cron expression with an Effect handler, deploy it, and prove the trigger fires with a bounded polling test.
- [React to GitHub events from a Worker](https://alchemy.run/cloudflare/messaging/github-events) — Subscribe a Cloudflare Worker to GitHub repository webhooks with typed payloads — alchemy provisions the webhook and verifies delivery signatures.
- [K2 streams](https://alchemy.run/cloudflare/messaging/k2) — Cloudflare K2 is a durable, replayable log. Produce records from Workers with the WriteStream binding, then consume them from a long-running host with consumeStreamRecords.
- [Queues](https://alchemy.run/cloudflare/messaging/queues) — How Cloudflare Queues carry messages from producer Workers to a consumer in batches, with retries and dead-letter queues, and how platform events like Workflow completions arrive on a Queue.

## Cloudflare — Email

- [Send & receive email](https://alchemy.run/cloudflare/email/send-and-receive) — Enable Email Routing on a zone, verify destination addresses, forward inbound mail with rules and a catch-all, and send email from a Worker with the send_email binding.
- [Receive email in a Worker](https://alchemy.run/cloudflare/email/email-worker) — Receive inbound mail in a Cloudflare Worker with Cloudflare.email({ zone }).subscribe(...) — auto-creates routing and forwarding rules.
- [Email](https://alchemy.run/cloudflare/email) — Cloudflare Email Routing turns a zone into a mail endpoint — enable routing, verify destinations, forward with rules and a catch-all, hand mail to a Worker, and send from Workers with the send_email binding.

## Cloudflare — AI

- [Run Workers AI models](https://alchemy.run/cloudflare/ai/workers-ai) — Bind Workers AI into your Worker with Cloudflare.Workers.AI — run inference and list models directly, or turn the binding into a typed Effect LanguageModel, no gateway required.
- [Effect AI](https://alchemy.run/cloudflare/ai/effect-ai) — Wire Effect's LanguageModel and Chat services into a Cloudflare Worker — read API keys with effect/Config, provide the model layer to your handler, plug in persistence.
- [Add an AI Gateway](https://alchemy.run/cloudflare/ai/ai-gateway) — Wire an AI Gateway into your Worker, turn it into a typed Effect LanguageModel, and run generations and streams through Workers AI with caching, rate limiting, and logs.
- [Add AI Search (AutoRAG)](https://alchemy.run/cloudflare/ai/ai-search) — Stand up a Cloudflare AI Search (AutoRAG) pipeline over an R2 bucket with one Search call, bind it into your Worker as a typed Effect client, and answer questions over your own documents.
- [Vector search with Vectorize](https://alchemy.run/cloudflare/ai/vectorize) — Create a Vectorize index, bind it to a Worker with SearchIndex, and run filtered nearest-neighbor queries over vector embeddings.

## Cloudflare — Security & secrets

- [Secrets Store & auth tokens](https://alchemy.run/cloudflare/security/secrets-store) — Store secrets in Cloudflare's account-level Secrets Store, generate stable tokens with Alchemy.Random, and read them in a Worker through the ReadSecret binding.
- [Protect a Worker with Access](https://alchemy.run/cloudflare/security/access) — Put Cloudflare Access in front of a Worker with the access prop — per-Worker policies, shared applications, ctx.access identity at runtime, and a local dev simulation.
- [Turnstile CAPTCHA](https://alchemy.run/cloudflare/security/turnstile) — Manage Cloudflare Turnstile widgets as resources — deploy a widget, embed its sitekey in HTML, and verify tokens server-side with the redacted secret.
- [Secrets & env](https://alchemy.run/cloudflare/security/secrets-env) — Bind env vars and secrets to Workers with effect/Config, generate stable tokens with Alchemy.Random, and graduate to Secrets Store when secrets are shared across Workers.

## Cloudflare — Observability

- [Native Workers tracing](https://alchemy.run/cloudflare/observability/workers-tracing) — Mirror Effect spans into Cloudflare Workers Observability with Cloudflare.Telemetry() — the same Layer shape as Axiom.Telemetry, with Cloudflare owning sampling and export.
- [Ship Worker telemetry to Axiom](https://alchemy.run/cloudflare/observability/axiom-observability) — Declare Axiom datasets, a least-privilege ingest token, and monitors in the same Stack as the Worker that emits the telemetry — or let Cloudflare push Workers Logs to Axiom natively.
- [Analytics Engine](https://alchemy.run/cloudflare/observability/analytics-engine) — Write time-series data points from a Worker with Workers Analytics Engine — declare a dataset, bind it with WriteDataset, and query it later over Cloudflare's SQL API.

## Cloudflare — Networking

- [Custom domains & routes](https://alchemy.run/cloudflare/networking/custom-domains) — Serve Workers from your own domain — create or adopt a Zone, attach custom domains, route hostname patterns, manage DNS records, and control the workers.dev subdomain.
- [Federated APIs](https://alchemy.run/cloudflare/networking/federated-apis) — Serve one API at one URL from many Workers — each path handled by its own least-privilege Worker, routed by Cloudflare's zone routes with no gateway Worker, and emulated locally by alchemy dev.
- [Expose private origins with Tunnel](https://alchemy.run/cloudflare/networking/tunnel) — Connect a private origin to Cloudflare's edge with a Tunnel, declare its ingress rules as a Configuration resource, and point DNS at it with a proxied CNAME.
- [Domains & DNS](https://alchemy.run/cloudflare/networking/domains) — Manage Cloudflare zones, DNS records, DNSSEC, and zone settings as resources — and safely adopt the domains you already have.

## AWS — start here

The AWS hub: overview, What is AWS? (accounts, regions, IAM, resources and ARNs, runtimes, bindings, event sources, VPCs, the edge and how Alchemy models each), the accounts-and-regions and IAM-and-bindings chapters, setup (credentials, profiles, region), local development, and the Lambda vs ECS vs EKS vs EC2 decision page.

- [AWS](https://alchemy.run/aws) — Build on AWS with Alchemy. Declare Lambda Functions, containers, tables, buckets and queues in TypeScript, and let bindings write each runtime's IAM policy from the calls its code makes.
- [What is AWS?](https://alchemy.run/aws/what-is-aws) — The concepts behind AWS — accounts, regions, IAM identities and policies, resources and ARNs, runtimes, event sources, VPCs and the edge — and how @alchemy.run/aws models each of them.
- [Accounts and regions](https://alchemy.run/aws/accounts-and-regions) — How AWS accounts isolate resources, how regions and Availability Zones place them, and how profiles and stages choose where each Alchemy deploy goes.
- [IAM and bindings](https://alchemy.run/aws/iam) — How IAM identities, roles, trust, resource-based policies and tag-based access (ABAC) work on AWS, and how Alchemy bindings write each runtime's least-privilege policies from the calls its code makes.
- [Setup](https://alchemy.run/aws/setup) — Connect Alchemy to AWS with SSO, console login, stored access keys, or CI environment credentials.
- [Local development](https://alchemy.run/aws/local-development) — alchemy dev runs your AWS stack on your machine — Lambda in Docker containers, local S3/DynamoDB/SQS, event sources firing, hot reload — with no AWS account or credentials required.
- [Choosing a runtime](https://alchemy.run/aws/compute/choosing-a-runtime) — How Lambda Functions, Lambda Web Functions, ECS, EKS and EC2 differ in how they run your code, scale and cost, and how to choose one for each part of an app.

## AWS — tutorial

A linear five-part walkthrough from zero to a tested, CI-deployed AWS project. Each part builds on the previous one.

- [Part 1: Your First Stack](https://alchemy.run/aws/tutorial/part-1) — Install Alchemy, create a Stack with an AWS S3 Bucket, and deploy it.
- [Part 2: Add a Lambda](https://alchemy.run/aws/tutorial/part-2) — Create an AWS Lambda Function with a public URL, bind the S3 Bucket, and implement GET/PUT routes.
- [Part 3: Testing](https://alchemy.run/aws/tutorial/part-3) — Write integration tests that deploy your stack and make HTTP requests against your live Lambda Function URL.
- [Part 4: Stages](https://alchemy.run/aws/tutorial/part-4) — Deploy isolated dev, staging, and prod instances of your stack with --stage, and tune resources per stage.
- [Part 5: CI/CD](https://alchemy.run/aws/tutorial/part-5) — Set up GitHub Actions for automated AWS deployments and PR previews — with OIDC credentials provisioned as code.

## AWS — Compute

- [Lambda MicroVMs](https://alchemy.run/aws/compute/microvms) — Build a Firecracker MicroVM image from TypeScript or a Dockerfile, then launch and drive isolated stateful instances from a Lambda Function with typed lifecycle bindings and RPC.
- [Nitro Sandboxes](https://alchemy.run/aws/compute/nitro-sandboxes) — How Nitro Sandboxes run each ECS task, EKS pod or self-managed workload in its own lightweight VM on your EC2 instances, the difference between isolated and confidential modes, and how to turn them on for ECS, EKS and EC2.
- [EC2](https://alchemy.run/aws/compute/ec2) — How EC2 instances give you a whole virtual machine, how to launch one from an image into a subnet, how to run your Effect program on it as a service, and how to reach it.
- [ECS](https://alchemy.run/aws/compute/ecs) — How ECS runs containers on Fargate through clusters, task definitions, tasks and services, and how to run a server, a one-off job or a scheduled job from an image, a Dockerfile or an Effect program.
- [ECS Sandboxes](https://alchemy.run/aws/compute/ecs-sandboxes) — Create a Nitro Sandbox per user or session on ECS from a Lambda Function, then run commands, use files, open terminals and call ports in it through a typed handle.
- [Effect workflows](https://alchemy.run/aws/compute/effect-workflows) — Run Effect workflows on AWS Lambda durable functions. Host them in an AWS.Lambda.WorkflowFunction, start runs from other functions with AWS.Lambda.DurableFunctionEngine, and let them sleep and wait durably.
- [EKS](https://alchemy.run/aws/compute/eks) — Stand up an EKS Auto Mode cluster on a Network and run containers on it — Deployments for servers, Jobs for run-to-completion work, Manifests for everything else. No YAML, no kubectl.
- [HyperPod](https://alchemy.run/aws/compute/hyperpod) — Provision SageMaker HyperPod clusters — Slurm or EKS orchestrated — and run ML workloads on them with sbatch, raw manifests, or effectful Jobs with task governance.
- [Lambda](https://alchemy.run/aws/compute/lambda) — How a Lambda Function runs your code per invocation, how it's invoked over a Function URL, by events or by other code, and how construction, timeouts and configuration work.
- [Lambda Web Functions](https://alchemy.run/aws/compute/web-functions) — Run an HTTP server on AWS Lambda Web Functions — an Effect fetch handler or any Node server, with streaming responses, many concurrent requests per environment, and a built-in HTTPS endpoint.

- [Next.js](https://alchemy.run/aws/frontend/nextjs) — Deploy a Next.js app to AWS with AWS.Website.Nextjs — Next's own server on a Lambda Web Function with a shared S3 cache, S3 assets behind CloudFront, and next dev under alchemy dev.

- [Nuxt](https://alchemy.run/aws/frontend/nuxt) — Deploy a Nuxt app to AWS with AWS.Website.Nuxt — the nitro server on a Lambda Web Function, S3 assets behind CloudFront, and Nuxt's own dev server under alchemy dev.
- [SolidStart](https://alchemy.run/aws/frontend/solidstart) — Deploy a SolidStart app to AWS with AWS.Website.SolidStart — SSR on a Lambda Web Function, S3 assets behind CloudFront, and SolidStart's own Vite dev server under alchemy dev.
- [Astro](https://alchemy.run/aws/frontend/astro) — Deploy an Astro app to AWS with AWS.Website.Astro — SSR on a Lambda Web Function, static output on S3 + CloudFront, and Astro's own dev server under alchemy dev.
- [SvelteKit](https://alchemy.run/aws/frontend/sveltekit) — Deploy a SvelteKit app to AWS with AWS.Website.SvelteKit — SSR on a Lambda Web Function, assets and prerendered pages on S3 + CloudFront, and Kit's own dev server under alchemy dev.

## AWS — Messaging & events

- [DynamoDB Streams](https://alchemy.run/aws/messaging/dynamodb-streams) — How a DynamoDB Stream records every change to a table in order, what each change record carries, and how a Function consumes changes and checkpoints at the first failure.
- [EventBridge & Scheduler](https://alchemy.run/aws/messaging/eventbridge) — How EventBridge buses route events to targets by matching their content, how runtimes publish and consume events, and how EventBridge Scheduler runs Functions, Queues and tasks on a schedule.
- [Kinesis](https://alchemy.run/aws/messaging/kinesis) — How Kinesis Data Streams keep records in order per partition key across shards, how runtimes write records and consume them in batches, and how retention, replay and checkpoints work.
- [S3 events](https://alchemy.run/aws/messaging/s3-events) — How a Bucket notifies a Function when objects are created or deleted, what each notification carries, and how to process notifications as an Effect Stream.
- [SNS](https://alchemy.run/aws/messaging/sns) — How SNS Topics broadcast one message to every subscriber, how to publish from a runtime, subscribe Functions and Queues, and filter what each subscriber receives.
- [SQS](https://alchemy.run/aws/messaging/sqs) — How SQS Queues hand work from producers to consumers, how visibility timeouts, retries and dead-letter queues keep messages from being lost, and how runtimes send to and consume from a Queue.

## GCP

Google Cloud as Stack resources — Cloud Run services and jobs, Firestore, Pub/Sub, BigQuery, Secret Manager, Memorystore. Bindings grant IAM onto a per-host service account.

- [Projects and regions](https://alchemy.run/gcp/projects-and-regions) — How GCP projects isolate resources and sit in an organization, how regions and zones place them, and how profiles and stages choose where each Alchemy deploy goes.
- [Setup](https://alchemy.run/gcp/setup) — Connect alchemy to Google Cloud — project, service-account key, the APIs to enable, and Docker.

## GCP — Compute

- [Choosing a runtime](https://alchemy.run/gcp/compute/choosing-a-runtime) — How Cloud Run services, jobs and worker pools, Cloud Functions and GKE differ in what triggers them, how they scale and what they cost, and how to choose one for each part of an app.
- [Cloud Functions](https://alchemy.run/gcp/compute/cloud-functions) — Deploy an Effect fetch handler as a 2nd-gen Cloud Function — built by Google from an uploaded bundle, so no local Docker is needed.
- [Cloud Run](https://alchemy.run/gcp/compute/cloud-run) — Run an Effect HTTP service on Cloud Run with GCP.Function — public or private URLs, environment, scaling, and bindings that grant IAM.
- [Cloud Run jobs](https://alchemy.run/gcp/compute/jobs) — Run batch work to completion with GCP.Run.Job — trigger it from a service with RunJob, or nightly with Cloud Scheduler.
- [Cloud Run sidecars](https://alchemy.run/gcp/compute/sidecars) — Run more containers next to a Cloud Run service — plain images, GCP.Run.Container resources, or your own Effect programs — and control the order they start in.
- [GKE](https://alchemy.run/gcp/compute/gke) — Run Effect programs as Kubernetes Deployments and Jobs on a GKE Autopilot cluster, with bindings granted through Workload Identity.
- [Worker pools](https://alchemy.run/gcp/compute/worker-pools) — Run always-on queue consumers with GCP.Run.WorkerPool — no URL, a fixed instance count, and a Pub/Sub pull loop.

## GCP — Frontend

- [Websites](https://alchemy.run/gcp/frontend/websites) — Deploy Vite, Astro, Next.js, Nuxt, SvelteKit, TanStack Start, React Router, SolidStart, Waku, vinext, Octane, Vocs, or any static build to Cloud Run with GCP.Website.
- [Vite](https://alchemy.run/gcp/frontend/vite) — Deploy any client-only Vite app to Cloud Run with GCP.Website.Vite — your own vite.config, a small static file server, and Vite's dev server under alchemy dev.
- [React SPA](https://alchemy.run/gcp/frontend/vite-spa) — Deploy a React single-page app to Cloud Run with GCP.Website.Vite — scaffold with Vite, deep links answered by index.html, Vite's dev server under alchemy dev.
- [Vue](https://alchemy.run/gcp/frontend/vue) — Deploy a Vue single-page app to Cloud Run with GCP.Website.Vite — scaffold with create-vue, deep links answered by index.html.
- [Foldkit](https://alchemy.run/gcp/frontend/foldkit) — Deploy a Foldkit app to Cloud Run with GCP.Website.Foldkit — a Vite build with deep links that boot the app.
- [Astro](https://alchemy.run/gcp/frontend/astro) — Deploy an Astro site to Cloud Run with GCP.Website.Astro — server-rendered pages, prerendered pages, and Astro's own dev server under alchemy dev.
- [Next.js](https://alchemy.run/gcp/frontend/nextjs) — Deploy a Next.js app to Cloud Run with GCP.Website.Nextjs — Next's own production server in a container, no OpenNext.
- [Nuxt](https://alchemy.run/gcp/frontend/nuxt) — Deploy a Nuxt app to Cloud Run with GCP.Website.Nuxt — the nitro Node server in a container, prerendered pages served as static files.
- [SvelteKit](https://alchemy.run/gcp/frontend/sveltekit) — Deploy a SvelteKit app to Cloud Run with GCP.Website.SvelteKit — kit's server in a container, static assets served first.
- [TanStack Start](https://alchemy.run/gcp/frontend/tanstack-start) — Deploy a TanStack Start app (React or Solid) to Cloud Run with GCP.Website.TanStackStart — your own vite build, served by a Node server.
- [React Router](https://alchemy.run/gcp/frontend/react-router) — Deploy a React Router v8 app in framework mode to Cloud Run with GCP.Website.ReactRouter.
- [SolidStart](https://alchemy.run/gcp/frontend/solidstart) — Deploy a SolidStart app to Cloud Run with GCP.Website.SolidStart — SSR in a container, prerendered pages served as static files.
- [Waku](https://alchemy.run/gcp/frontend/waku) — Deploy a Waku (React Server Components) app to Cloud Run with GCP.Website.Waku.
- [vinext](https://alchemy.run/gcp/frontend/vinext) — Deploy a vinext app (the Next.js API on Vite) to Cloud Run with GCP.Website.Vinext.
- [Octane](https://alchemy.run/gcp/frontend/octane) — Deploy an OctaneJS app to Cloud Run with GCP.Website.Octane.
- [Vocs](https://alchemy.run/gcp/frontend/vocs) — Deploy a Vocs documentation site to Cloud Run with GCP.Website.Vocs.
- [Static sites](https://alchemy.run/gcp/frontend/static-site) — Deploy Hugo, Zola, or any static build to Google Cloud — on Cloud Run with GCP.Website.StaticSite, or from a public Cloud Storage bucket.

## GCP — APIs

- [Effect HTTP API on Cloud Run](https://alchemy.run/gcp/apis/effect-http-api) — Build a schema-validated HTTP API with Effect's HttpApi module, deploy it to Cloud Run, and call it from a typed client.
- [Effect RPC on Cloud Run](https://alchemy.run/gcp/apis/effect-rpc) — Build a typed RPC API with Effect's Rpc module, deploy it to Cloud Run, and call its procedures from a typed client.

## GCP — Data

- [BigQuery](https://alchemy.run/gcp/data/bigquery) — Create BigQuery datasets and tables, stream rows in, and run parameterized queries from Cloud Run with ReadTable and WriteTable bindings.
- [Cloud SQL](https://alchemy.run/gcp/data/cloud-sql) — Run Postgres on Cloud SQL, connect Cloud Run to it over the Cloud SQL socket with GCP.SQL.Connect, and query it with Drizzle.
- [Cloud Storage](https://alchemy.run/gcp/data/storage) — Create Cloud Storage buckets, read and write objects from Cloud Run with Read, Write, and ReadWrite bindings, and hand out signed download URLs.
- [Firestore](https://alchemy.run/gcp/data/firestore) — Create a Firestore database and read and write documents from Cloud Run with typed Read, Write, and ReadWrite bindings.
- [Memorystore](https://alchemy.run/gcp/data/memorystore) — Create a Memorystore for Redis instance and reach it from Cloud Run over Direct VPC egress with the ReadWriteRedis binding.

## GCP — AI

- [Vertex AI](https://alchemy.run/gcp/ai/vertex-ai) — Call Gemini on Vertex AI from Cloud Run with the GenerateContent binding — no API key, just the service's own identity.

## GCP — Messaging & events

- [Cloud Scheduler](https://alchemy.run/gcp/messaging/scheduler) — Run code on a cron schedule with GCP.CloudScheduler.consumeSchedule — the handler lives on your Cloud Run service and only Cloud Scheduler can call it.
- [Eventarc](https://alchemy.run/gcp/messaging/eventarc) — React to Firestore changes, Cloud Storage events, and audit-logged Google API calls with GCP.Eventarc.consumeEvents.
- [Pub/Sub](https://alchemy.run/gcp/messaging/pubsub) — Publish to Pub/Sub topics from Cloud Run, consume them with push delivery or a pull loop, filter by attribute, and dead-letter failures.
- [Storage events](https://alchemy.run/gcp/messaging/storage-events) — Run code when an object lands in a Cloud Storage bucket with GCP.Storage.consumeBucketEvents.

## GCP — Security & secrets

- [Federated identity](https://alchemy.run/gcp/security/federated-identity) — How a Lambda or Fly Service reaches GCP, and a Cloud Run service reaches AWS, through workload identity federation instead of long-lived keys.
- [IAM & bindings](https://alchemy.run/gcp/security/iam) — What a GCP binding does — the per-runtime service account, the role it grants, where the grant lands, and how removing a binding revokes it.
- [Secret Manager & KMS](https://alchemy.run/gcp/security/secrets-kms) — Keep API keys in Secret Manager and read them per request, encrypt data with Cloud KMS, and pass plain config through env.

## GCP — Observability

- [Logging & Monitoring](https://alchemy.run/gcp/observability/monitoring) — Declare uptime checks, alert policies, notification channels, and logs-based metrics in the same Stack as the services they watch.

## GCP — Networking

- [Private services](https://alchemy.run/gcp/networking/private-services) — Keep a Cloud Run service private and call it from another service with GCP.Run.InvokeService and Google-signed identity tokens.
- [VPC & private networking](https://alchemy.run/gcp/networking/vpc) — Give Cloud Run services Direct VPC egress to reach private IPs like Memorystore, and create your own VPC networks and subnets.

## Fly — start here

The Fly hub: overview, What is Fly? (organizations, Apps, Machines, regions, the proxy, private networking, Volumes, managed data and how Alchemy models each), setup (org, API token, profile), and networking.

- [Fly](https://alchemy.run/fly) — Run Effect programs on Fly.io with Alchemy. Declare Services, Machines, Volumes, Postgres, Redis and Tigris in TypeScript, in the regions near your users.
- [What is Fly?](https://alchemy.run/fly/what-is-fly) — The concepts behind Fly.io — organizations, Apps, Machines, regions, the Fly proxy, private networking, Volumes, managed data, secrets and certificates — and how @alchemy.run/fly models each of them.
- [Organizations and tokens](https://alchemy.run/fly/organizations-and-tokens) — How a Fly organization holds your Apps and billing, how an organization token decides where Alchemy deploys, and how to keep production in its own organization.
- [Federated identity](https://alchemy.run/fly/federated-identity) — How a Fly Service reaches AWS and GCP with the OIDC tokens its Machines sign, instead of a stored access key or service account key.
- [Setup](https://alchemy.run/fly/setup) — Create a Fly org, generate an API token, and store it in a profile.
- [IPs & certificates](https://alchemy.run/fly/networking) — Public and private Fly Services, App addresses, and certificates for your own hostname.

## Fly — Tutorial

- [Part 1: Your First Service](https://alchemy.run/fly/tutorial/part-1) — Install Alchemy, create a Stack, and deploy an Effect HTTP Service to Fly on its own fly.dev hostname.
- [Part 2: Configure the Service](https://alchemy.run/fly/tutorial/part-2) — Pin the Service's region and port, add a health route, and ship a code change.
- [Part 3: Persist Data with a Volume](https://alchemy.run/fly/tutorial/part-3) — Mount a Fly disk into your Service with MountVolume and store files that survive deploys.
- [Part 4: Secrets and Cleanup](https://alchemy.run/fly/tutorial/part-4) — Read a secret from .env in the Service with Config.Redacted, guard a route with it, and destroy the stack.

## Fly — Compute

- [Apps](https://alchemy.run/fly/compute/apps) — A global namespace containing Machines, Services, Secrets, IPs, and certificates.
- [Blue/green deployments](https://alchemy.run/fly/compute/deployments) — Deploy a new version, check it before serving traffic, and give the old version time to finish work.
- [Connect Services](https://alchemy.run/fly/compute/connecting-services) — Build several Fly Services that call each other's methods over a private network, behind one public entry point.
- [Machines](https://alchemy.run/fly/compute/machines) — A Firecracker VM running a container image.
- [Regions](https://alchemy.run/fly/compute/regions) — Where Fly Machines, Volumes, Postgres, and Redis live. Alchemy defaults to iad.
- [Services](https://alchemy.run/fly/compute/services) — An Effect program running in Fly Machines in its own Fly App. Scale it with count.
- [Sprites](https://alchemy.run/fly/compute/sprites) — An Effect program running in a Fly.io Sprite. It hibernates when idle.

## Fly — Data

- [Drizzle Postgres on Fly](https://alchemy.run/fly/data/drizzle-postgres) — Connect a Fly Service to Managed Postgres and deploy reviewed Drizzle migrations.
- [Postgres](https://alchemy.run/fly/data/postgres) — A billed Managed Postgres cluster. Bind Fly.ConnectPostgres and query with Drizzle or SQL.
- [Redis](https://alchemy.run/fly/data/redis) — Managed Upstash Redis. Bind Fly.ReadRedis / WriteRedis / ReadWriteRedis on a Service.
- [Secrets](https://alchemy.run/fly/data/secrets) — Config.Redacted on a Service, Fly.Secret when Fly should own the value, and KMS keys.
- [Tigris](https://alchemy.run/fly/data/tigris) — S3-compatible object storage billed through Fly. Bind Fly.PutObject / Fly.GetObject.
- [Volumes](https://alchemy.run/fly/data/volumes) — A disk in one region, attached to one Machine.

- [Static sites](https://alchemy.run/fly/frontend/static-site) — Deploy a static site to Fly with Fly.Website.StaticSite — a build command, a Node static-file server on a Machine, and https://{app}.fly.dev (or your hostname) on deploy.

- [Foldkit](https://alchemy.run/fly/frontend/foldkit) — Deploy Foldkit SPA, SSR, SSG, and hybrid applications to Fly with native local development.
- [TanStack Start](https://alchemy.run/fly/frontend/tanstack-start) — Deploy TanStack Start (React or Solid) to Fly with Fly.Website.TanStackStart — SSR on a Machine, client assets baked into the image, and TanStack Start's own Vite dev server under alchemy dev.
- [Next.js](https://alchemy.run/fly/frontend/nextjs) — Deploy a Next.js app to Fly with Fly.Website.Nextjs — next build plus a Node next({ dev: false }) Machine, and next dev under alchemy dev.
- [Vinext](https://alchemy.run/fly/frontend/vinext) — Deploy vinext to Fly with the shared Website API, native local development, and a platform-specific data cache.
- [Nuxt](https://alchemy.run/fly/frontend/nuxt) — Deploy a Nuxt app to Fly with Fly.Website.Nuxt — nitro's node preset on a Machine, assets baked into the image, and Nuxt's own dev server under alchemy dev.
- [Vocs](https://alchemy.run/fly/frontend/vocs) — Deploy a Vocs docs site to Fly with Fly.Website.Vocs — prerendered HTML on a Node static-file server, extensionless routes, and Vocs' own dev server under alchemy dev.
- [SolidStart](https://alchemy.run/fly/frontend/solidstart) — Deploy a SolidStart app to Fly with Fly.Website.SolidStart — nitro's node preset on a Machine, prerendered pages baked into the image, and SolidStart's own Vite dev server under alchemy dev.
- [Astro](https://alchemy.run/fly/frontend/astro) — Deploy an Astro app to Fly with Fly.Website.Astro — Node SSR on a Machine, static output as a file server, and Astro's own dev server under alchemy dev.
- [SvelteKit](https://alchemy.run/fly/frontend/sveltekit) — Deploy a SvelteKit app to Fly with Fly.Website.SvelteKit — kit SSR on a Machine, prerendered assets baked into the image, and Kit's own dev server under alchemy dev.
- [Waku](https://alchemy.run/fly/frontend/waku) — Deploy a Waku app to Fly with Fly.Website.Waku — RSC server on a Machine, SSG pages baked into the image, and Waku's own dev server under alchemy dev.
- [Octane](https://alchemy.run/fly/frontend/octane) — Deploy an OctaneJS app to Fly with Fly.Website.Octane — SSR on a Machine, client assets baked into the image, and Octane's own Vite dev server under alchemy dev.

- [Projects, tokens and SSH keys](https://alchemy.run/hetzner/projects-and-tokens) — How a Hetzner Cloud project isolates your Servers, how its API token decides where Alchemy deploys, and how SSH keys reach your Servers.

## Railway — start here

The Railway hub: overview, What is Railway? (workspaces, projects, environments, services, databases, volumes, variables, networking and how Alchemy models each), setup (workspace, API token, profile), and networking.

- [Railway](https://alchemy.run/railway) — Run Effect programs on Railway with Alchemy. Declare Projects, Services, Functions, Postgres, MySQL, Redis, Volumes and Buckets in one TypeScript program.
- [What is Railway?](https://alchemy.run/railway/what-is-railway) — The concepts behind Railway — workspaces, projects, environments, services, deployments, databases, volumes, variables, private networking and domains — and how @alchemy.run/railway models each of them.
- [Workspaces and tokens](https://alchemy.run/railway/workspaces-and-tokens) — How a Railway workspace holds your projects and billing, which tokens Alchemy can deploy with, and how to keep production apart.
- [Setup](https://alchemy.run/railway/setup) — Create a Railway workspace, generate an account API token, and store it in a profile.
- [Custom domains, TCP & private networks](https://alchemy.run/railway/networking) — Reach a Railway Service on your own hostname, expose databases over public TCP, and name private-mesh DNS.

## Railway — Tutorial

- [Part 1: Your First Project](https://alchemy.run/railway/tutorial/part-1) — Install Alchemy, create a Stack with a Railway Project, and deploy it.
- [Part 2: Deploy a Service](https://alchemy.run/railway/tutorial/part-2) — Bundle an Effect HTTP server, deploy it to Railway as a Service, and serve requests on up.railway.app.
- [Part 3: Persist Data with a Volume](https://alchemy.run/railway/tutorial/part-3) — Mount a Railway disk into your Service with MountVolume and store files that survive deploys.
- [Part 4: Variables and Cleanup](https://alchemy.run/railway/tutorial/part-4) — Store a Project variable, read it from the Service at runtime, and destroy the stack.

## Railway — Compute

- [Environments](https://alchemy.run/railway/compute/environments) — Extra deploy environments under a Project. Production is created with the Project — do not duplicate it.
- [Functions, templates & VMs](https://alchemy.run/railway/compute/functions) — Effect-native canvas Functions, marketplace templates, sandboxes, and cloud agents on Railway.
- [Projects](https://alchemy.run/railway/compute/projects) — A workspace-scoped namespace containing Services, Environments, Volumes, Variables, and Buckets.
- [Regions](https://alchemy.run/railway/compute/regions) — Where Railway Services, Volumes, Postgres, and Buckets live.
- [Services](https://alchemy.run/railway/compute/services) — A container in a Railway Project — a public image, or an Effect program Railway builds from a generated Dockerfile.

## Railway — Data

- [Buckets](https://alchemy.run/railway/data/buckets) — S3-compatible object storage in a Project. Bind Railway.PutObject / Railway.GetObject.
- [Drizzle MySQL on Railway](https://alchemy.run/railway/data/drizzle-mysql) — Connect an Effect-native Railway Service to MySQL and deploy committed Drizzle migrations.
- [Drizzle Postgres on Railway](https://alchemy.run/railway/data/drizzle-postgres) — Query Railway Postgres from an Effect-native Service and apply reviewed Drizzle migrations separately.
- [Mongo](https://alchemy.run/railway/data/mongo) — Official MongoDB in a Project. Bind Railway.ConnectMongo and ping with the MongoDB driver.
- [MySQL](https://alchemy.run/railway/data/mysql) — Official MySQL in a Project. Bind Railway.ConnectMySQL and query with Drizzle or SQL.
- [Postgres](https://alchemy.run/railway/data/postgres) — Official SSL Postgres in a Project. Bind Railway.ConnectPostgres and query with Drizzle or SQL.
- [Redis](https://alchemy.run/railway/data/redis) — Redis in a Project. Bind Railway.ReadRedis / WriteRedis / ReadWriteRedis on a Service.
- [Variables](https://alchemy.run/railway/data/variables) — Config.Redacted on a Service, Railway.Variable when Railway should own the value.
- [Volumes](https://alchemy.run/railway/data/volumes) — Block disk in a Project. Mount it into a Service with MountVolume.

- [Static sites](https://alchemy.run/railway/frontend/static-site) — Deploy a static site to Railway with Railway.Website.StaticSite — a build command, a container Service.
- [React Router](https://alchemy.run/railway/frontend/react-router) — Deploy React Router v8 (framework mode) to Railway with Railway.Website.ReactRouter — SSR on a container Service, client assets in the image, and React Router's own Vite dev server under alchemy dev.
- [Foldkit](https://alchemy.run/railway/frontend/foldkit) — Deploy Foldkit SPA, SSR, SSG, and hybrid applications to Railway with native local development.
- [TanStack Start](https://alchemy.run/railway/frontend/tanstack-start) — Deploy TanStack Start (React or Solid) to Railway with Railway.Website.TanStackStart — SSR on a container Service, client assets in the image, and TanStack Start's own Vite dev server under alchemy dev.
- [Next.js](https://alchemy.run/railway/frontend/nextjs) — Deploy a Next.js app to Railway with Railway.Website.Nextjs — next build plus a Node next({ dev: false }) container, and next dev under alchemy dev.
- [Vinext](https://alchemy.run/railway/frontend/vinext) — Deploy vinext to Railway with the shared Website API, native local development, and a platform-specific data cache.
- [Nuxt](https://alchemy.run/railway/frontend/nuxt) — Deploy a Nuxt app to Railway with Railway.Website.Nuxt — nitro's node preset on a Service, and Nuxt's own dev server under alchemy dev.
- [Vocs](https://alchemy.run/railway/frontend/vocs) — Deploy a Vocs docs site to Railway with Railway.Website.Vocs — prerendered HTML on a Railway Service, extensionless routes, and Vocs' own dev server under alchemy dev.
- [SolidStart](https://alchemy.run/railway/frontend/solidstart) — Deploy a SolidStart app to Railway with Railway.Website.SolidStart — nitro's node preset on a container Service, prerendered pages in the image, and SolidStart's own Vite dev server under alchemy dev.
- [Astro](https://alchemy.run/railway/frontend/astro) — Deploy an Astro app to Railway with Railway.Website.Astro — Node SSR on a Service container, static output as a file server, and Astro's own dev server under alchemy dev.
- [SvelteKit](https://alchemy.run/railway/frontend/sveltekit) — Deploy a SvelteKit app to Railway with Railway.Website.SvelteKit — kit SSR plus prerendered assets on one Service, and Kit's own dev server under alchemy dev.
- [Waku](https://alchemy.run/railway/frontend/waku) — Deploy a Waku app to Railway with Railway.Website.Waku — RSC server on a container Service, SSG pages in the image, and Waku's own dev server under alchemy dev.
- [Octane](https://alchemy.run/railway/frontend/octane) — Deploy an OctaneJS app to Railway with Railway.Website.Octane — SSR plus client assets on one Service, and Octane's own Vite dev server under alchemy dev.

## PlanetScale

Serverless MySQL & Postgres as Stack resources. Composes with Cloudflare Hyperdrive and Drizzle — those guides are listed under Cloudflare.

- [PlanetScale](https://alchemy.run/planetscale) — Declare PlanetScale Postgres and MySQL databases, branches and credentials in your Stack with Alchemy, apply migrations on deploy, and give every preview stage its own branch.
- [What is PlanetScale?](https://alchemy.run/planetscale/what-is-planetscale) — The concepts behind PlanetScale — organizations, databases, the Postgres and Vitess engines, cluster sizes, branches, credentials, connections, migrations and backups — and how @alchemy.run/planetscale models each of them.
- [Organizations and tokens](https://alchemy.run/planetscale/organizations-and-tokens) — How a PlanetScale organization holds your databases and members, how Alchemy signs in with OAuth or a service token, and how database credentials differ from deploy credentials.
- [Setup](https://alchemy.run/planetscale/setup) — Connect alchemy to PlanetScale — account, credentials, and profiles.
- [Postgres](https://alchemy.run/planetscale/data/postgres) — PlanetScale Postgres as Stack resources — databases, branches, roles with least-privilege inherited roles, and direct vs pooled connection origins.
- [MySQL](https://alchemy.run/planetscale/data/mysql) — PlanetScale MySQL (Vitess) as Stack resources — databases, branches, and passwords, with SQL migrations per branch and a straight line into Cloudflare Hyperdrive.
- [Migrations](https://alchemy.run/planetscale/data/migrations) — Apply SQL migrations and seed data to PlanetScale databases and branches as part of every deploy — ordered, hashed, tracked, and run over short-lived credentials.
- [Credentials](https://alchemy.run/planetscale/data/credentials) — PlanetScale credentials as Stack resources — Postgres roles, the default role and forceReset, MySQL passwords, TTLs, CIDR allowlists, and direct vs pooled connection origins.
- [Backups & restores](https://alchemy.run/planetscale/data/backups) — Restore a PlanetScale backup into a fresh branch with backupId, or seed a new branch from the last successful backup with seedData.
- [Preview branches per PR](https://alchemy.run/planetscale/guides/preview-branches) — Give every pull request its own PlanetScale branch — a long-lived database owned by a staging stage, referenced by ephemeral PR stages that fork, migrate, and tear down a branch each.
- [Drizzle ORM with PlanetScale](https://alchemy.run/planetscale/guides/drizzle) — Configure PlanetScale Postgres or MySQL branches, committed Drizzle migrations, and role or password connections.

## Neon

Neon backend resources: Postgres branches, Functions, private object storage, managed Auth, Data API, AI Gateway and Website adapters. The upload tutorial combines native and Effect handlers with authenticated browser uploads.

- [Neon](https://alchemy.run/neon) — Declare Neon Postgres projects, branches and roles, plus Functions, storage, Auth, the Data API and AI Gateway, in an Alchemy Stack, with a branch per preview stage.
- [What is Neon?](https://alchemy.run/neon/what-is-neon) — The concepts behind Neon — organizations, projects, branches, computes, roles, connections, migrations, and the Functions, storage, Auth, Data API and AI Gateway around them — and how @alchemy.run/neon models each of them.
- [Setup](https://alchemy.run/neon/setup) — Prepare Neon credentials, service access, regions, and external dependencies before deploying with Alchemy.
- [Organizations and keys](https://alchemy.run/neon/organizations-and-keys) — How a Neon organization holds your projects and their branches, how an API key and orgId decide where Alchemy deploys, and why apps connect with their own credentials.
- [Functions](https://alchemy.run/neon/functions) — How Neon Functions run Node.js Fetch handlers next to a branch's database, in native or Effect form, how they subscribe to uploads and schedules, and why every handler authenticates its callers.
- [Storage](https://alchemy.run/neon/storage) — How Neon Buckets store files on a branch through an S3-compatible API, how typed Objects hold configuration as values, and how Functions read and write them through bindings.
- [Organization governance](https://alchemy.run/neon/governance) — Manage existing Neon organization access, billing alerts, and private-network associations with explicit ownership and restoration.
- [AI Gateway setup](https://alchemy.run/neon/guides/ai-gateway) — Buy Neon AI Gateway credits and use a model from an Effect Function.
- [Production Auth](https://alchemy.run/neon/guides/production-auth) — Configure trusted origins, SMTP, OAuth callbacks, and verification before launching Managed Better Auth.
- [Private networking](https://alchemy.run/neon/guides/private-networking) — Prepare AWS PrivateLink endpoints, register them with Neon, enable private DNS, and verify database access.
- [Custom domains](https://alchemy.run/neon/guides/custom-domains) — Register a Function hostname, configure DNS and CAA, verify HTTPS, and retire the domain safely.
- [State and recovery](https://alchemy.run/neon/guides/state-recovery) — Preserve Neon ownership and reveal-once secrets, recover interrupted deployments, and clean up without discarding state.
- [Build an upload journal](https://alchemy.run/neon/tutorial) — Sign in, upload private files, process real storage events, and view Postgres-backed status with Neon and Alchemy.
- [Create the upload backend](https://alchemy.run/neon/tutorial/backend) — Add a Neon project, a migrated branch, private storage, and managed authentication.
- [Protect and process uploads](https://alchemy.run/neon/tutorial/functions) — Verify JWTs, sign private uploads, and record real bucket events in Postgres.
- [Connect the browser](https://alchemy.run/neon/tutorial/frontend) — Use managed signup and sessions to upload and download private files from Vite.
- [Fork a preview and clean up](https://alchemy.run/neon/tutorial/previews) — Keep preview writes isolated from the parent, verify inheritance, and destroy only owned resources.
- [Branching](https://alchemy.run/neon/data/branching) — Neon branches are copy-on-write forks of a parent branch — create them per stage or preview, pin them to a point in time, copy schema only, and let them expire on their own.
- [Connections](https://alchemy.run/neon/data/connections) — Every Neon project and branch exposes direct and pooled connection URIs plus pre-parsed origin outputs — feed the direct origin to Hyperdrive and the pooled one to everything else.
- [Roles](https://alchemy.run/neon/data/roles) — Create Postgres roles on a Neon branch with Neon.Role — separate logins for your app and your migrations, with passwords as Redacted outputs.
- [Migrations](https://alchemy.run/neon/data/migrations) — Apply SQL migrations and seed data to Neon projects and branches as part of every deploy — ordered, hashed, and tracked in Alchemy's __alchemy_migrations table.
- [Preview branches per PR](https://alchemy.run/neon/guides/preview-branches) — Keep one long-lived Neon project in a staging stage and fork a copy-on-write branch per PR stage — isolated preview databases in seconds, destroyed with the stage.
- [Drizzle ORM with Neon](https://alchemy.run/neon/guides/drizzle) — Configure Neon projects, branches, committed Drizzle migrations, and direct or pooled connections.

E2B sandboxes for agents: what E2B is, team and API keys, network rules and egress secrets, templates, sandboxes from any Worker, warm snapshots and forks, programs baked into templates, volumes, and lifecycle events.

- [Team & API keys](https://alchemy.run/e2b/api-keys) — How an E2B team holds your templates and sandboxes, how your profile picks the team Alchemy deploys to, and what key each host gets instead of yours.
- [Network & secrets](https://alchemy.run/e2b/network-and-secrets) — Limit where a sandbox can connect, and add credentials to its requests without the sandbox seeing them.
- [Templates](https://alchemy.run/e2b/templates) — Build the images your sandboxes boot from, from a registry image, a Dockerfile, or another template.
- [Sandboxes](https://alchemy.run/e2b/sandboxes) — Create sandboxes from a Worker, run commands, read and write files, and manage their lifecycle.
- [Snapshots & forks](https://alchemy.run/e2b/snapshots) — Start sandboxes from a warm base, snapshot a running sandbox, and fork one into copies.
- [Template programs](https://alchemy.run/e2b/programs) — Run your own Effect program, or a plain JavaScript program, in every sandbox.
- [Volumes](https://alchemy.run/e2b/volumes) — Keep files that outlive sandboxes, mount them by name, and read or write them without a sandbox.
- [Lifecycle events](https://alchemy.run/e2b/lifecycle-events) — Handle sandbox lifecycle events in a Worker as E2B sends them.

## Archil — start here

Archil runs commands, processes and programs against durable disks in Firecracker microVMs: serverless exec, sandboxes, programs and websites, branches, and mounts in your own Containers and ECS tasks.

- [Archil](https://alchemy.run/archil) — Run commands, processes and programs serverlessly against durable disks, in Firecracker microVMs, with Alchemy. Declare disks, sandboxes, images and branches in TypeScript.
- [What is Archil?](https://alchemy.run/archil/what-is-archil) — The concepts behind Archil — organizations and API keys, regions, disks, serverless exec, sandboxes, images, mounts, disk users, branches and egress policy — and how @alchemy.run/archil models each of them.
- [Setup](https://alchemy.run/archil/setup) — Install the Archil provider, create an API key, and store it in a profile.

## Archil — Tutorial

- [Part 1: Set Up a Sandbox](https://alchemy.run/archil/tutorial/part-1) — Install Alchemy, and declare an Archil sandbox that clones a repository onto its disk at deploy time.
- [Part 2: Fork It for Each Request](https://alchemy.run/archil/tutorial/part-2) — A program in its own Archil sandbox that forks the set-up sandbox for each request, runs a command, and deletes the fork.
- [Part 3: A Fork per User](https://alchemy.run/archil/tutorial/part-3) — Give each user an Archil fork of the set-up sandbox, found again by name, which keeps their changes.
- [Part 4: Update the Sandbox](https://alchemy.run/archil/tutorial/part-4) — Change the commands that set up the Archil sandbox, redeploy, and see new forks start from the new one while existing forks keep theirs.
- [Part 5: Testing](https://alchemy.run/archil/tutorial/part-5) — Deploy the Stack in a test, fork the set-up sandbox, and check what the fork contains.
- [Part 6: Stages and CI](https://alchemy.run/archil/tutorial/part-6) — Deploy a stage per environment and per pull request, each with its own set-up Archil sandbox and program, from GitHub Actions.

## Archil — Accounts & access

- [Organization and keys](https://alchemy.run/archil/organization-and-keys) — How an Archil account or organization holds your disks, sandboxes and images, how an API key decides where Alchemy deploys, and what access each host gets instead of your key.
- [Credentials and bindings](https://alchemy.run/archil/security/credentials) — What each host gets to reach Archil, deploy-time resources vs run-time clients, and who owns what your app creates.
- [Network](https://alchemy.run/archil/security/network) — Control what a sandbox can reach, and add credentials to its requests on the way out.

## Archil — Compute

- [Choosing a runtime](https://alchemy.run/archil/compute/choosing-a-runtime) — Serverless exec, program sandboxes, sandboxes created at run time, and mounts on your own hosts, and when to use each.
- [Programs](https://alchemy.run/archil/compute/programs) — Run your program in its own Archil sandbox, in the Effect or async form, at a public https URL.
- [Sandboxes](https://alchemy.run/archil/compute/sandboxes) — Firecracker microVMs with disks mounted, declared as a dev box or created per task.
- [Images](https://alchemy.run/archil/compute/images) — Boot sandboxes from public images, private registries, or a Dockerfile built on your machine and pushed for Archil to pull.

## Archil — Storage

- [Disks](https://alchemy.run/archil/storage/disks) — Create disks per user at run time, share a few at deploy time, run commands against them, and read their files by key.
- [Mounting](https://alchemy.run/archil/storage/mounting) — Mount Archil disks in program sandboxes, your own Containers, and ECS tasks.
- [Branches and checkpoints](https://alchemy.run/archil/storage/branches) — Seed a disk once, checkpoint it at deploy time, and copy a writable branch per session in milliseconds.
- [Your own bucket](https://alchemy.run/archil/storage/your-own-bucket) — Keep a disk's files as ordinary objects in your own S3, R2, GCS or Azure bucket, with no keys for S3.
