## Rivet

Durable Objects on Rivet: a control plane and pools of nodes you run on Docker, AWS, GCP, Kubernetes, Fly, Hetzner or Railway (or Rivet Cloud), with key-value storage, SQL and alarms, called by name from any runtime.

- [Rivet](https://alchemy.run/rivet) — Build on Rivet with Alchemy. Declare Durable Objects and Durable Streams in TypeScript, run the control plane and its nodes on the cloud you choose or on Rivet Cloud, and call any instance by name from any runtime.
- [What is Rivet?](https://alchemy.run/rivet/what-is-rivet) — The concepts behind Rivet — Actors, one instance per name, state that lives with it, sleeping and waking, calls, the control plane, namespaces, pools, the gateway, Rivet Services and Rivet Cloud — and how @alchemy.run/rivet models each of them.
- [Setup](https://alchemy.run/rivet/setup) — Install the Rivet provider, the provider for the cloud you run it on, and get Docker ready to run Rivet on your machine.
- [Control planes and namespaces](https://alchemy.run/rivet/namespaces) — What holds a Rivet app — a control plane you run or Rivet Cloud, divided into namespaces — how Alchemy gives each stage its own namespace, and when to give an environment a control plane of its own.
- [Tokens and networks](https://alchemy.run/rivet/tokens-and-networks) — Who can reach a Rivet control plane and with what — the admin token and everything that holds it, the HTTPS address each control plane gets without a domain, nodes that only connect out, and the credentials a deploy needs in CI.
- [Secrets](https://alchemy.run/rivet/secrets) — Give a Rivet Durable Object an API key or a password with Config, hand a control plane its object storage keys, and choose where each stage's values come from.
- [Part 1: Your First Durable Object](https://alchemy.run/rivet/tutorial/part-1) — Run a Rivet control plane and pool on Docker, and deploy a chat room that counts its visitors.
- [Part 2: Messages in SQL](https://alchemy.run/rivet/tutorial/part-2) — Give each room a SQL table of messages, and post and read them over HTTP.
- [Part 3: Clear Idle Rooms](https://alchemy.run/rivet/tutorial/part-3) — Use a Durable Object alarm to clear a room's messages an hour after the last one.
- [Part 4: Run It on Hetzner](https://alchemy.run/rivet/tutorial/part-4) — Move the chat rooms from Docker to Hetzner Cloud by swapping the control plane, the pool and the API's host.
- [Four ways to build Actors](https://alchemy.run/rivet/actors) — Build Rivet Actors as Alchemy Durable Objects, with RivetKit, with RivetKit's Effect SDK, or in Rust — what each one is for, and how all four deploy to the same control planes and pools.
- [Durable Object](https://alchemy.run/rivet/durable-objects) — What a Rivet Durable Object is — a class with one instance per name, each with its own state — and how one is written, from its two phases and methods to fetch, alarm, and keeping its code out of its callers.
- [Storage](https://alchemy.run/rivet/storage) — What each Rivet Durable Object instance keeps — key-value entries, a SQL database and one alarm — and how to change it safely.
- [Concurrency](https://alchemy.run/rivet/concurrency) — How a Rivet Durable Object runs calls in parallel, how a transaction keeps a read and a write together, and how Workers.InputGate gives code written for Cloudflare the same rule it has there.
- [Calling a Durable Object](https://alchemy.run/rivet/calling) — How any runtime calls a Rivet Durable Object by name — methods, streams, typed errors, HTTP requests, and calls from one Durable Object to another.
- [RivetKit Actors](https://alchemy.run/rivet/rivetkit) — Deploy Actors written with RivetKit, unchanged, to a Rivet control plane and pool on any cloud.
- [RivetKit Effect Actors](https://alchemy.run/rivet/rivetkit-effect) — Deploy Actors written with RivetKit's Effect SDK, unchanged, to a Rivet control plane and pool on any cloud.
- [Rust Actors](https://alchemy.run/rivet/rivetkit-rust) — Deploy Actors written with RivetKit's Rust SDK, unchanged, to a Rivet control plane and pool. Alchemy compiles the crate into the pool's node image.
- [Durable Streams](https://alchemy.run/rivet/durable-streams) — Append-only logs with a replayable history, one per key, served by Rivet Services — declare one with its message Schema, append, read from an offset, follow it live, and choose its wire format as a Layer.
- [Control Plane](https://alchemy.run/rivet/control-planes) — What a Rivet control plane does, how to run one as a Layer on any cloud, how many engines it needs, and how to use one you already have.
- [Pool](https://alchemy.run/rivet/pools) — How a Rivet pool decides which machines run your Durable Objects, and when to share a pool, split one, or scale it.
- [Docker](https://alchemy.run/rivet/docker) — Run a Rivet control plane and pools of nodes on a Docker swarm, on your machine or a server.
- [AWS](https://alchemy.run/rivet/aws) — Run a Rivet control plane on EC2 or ECS, and pools of nodes on Fargate or EC2.
- [GCP](https://alchemy.run/rivet/gcp) — Run a Rivet control plane on Compute Engine, and pools of nodes on Cloud Run or Compute Engine.
- [Kubernetes](https://alchemy.run/rivet/kubernetes) — Run a Rivet control plane and pools of nodes on any Kubernetes cluster — EKS, GKE, kind or your own.
- [Fly](https://alchemy.run/rivet/fly) — Run a Rivet control plane on Fly Machines and pools of nodes on a Fly Service.
- [Hetzner](https://alchemy.run/rivet/hetzner) — Run a Rivet control plane and pools of nodes on Hetzner Cloud Servers.
- [Railway](https://alchemy.run/rivet/railway) — Run pools of Rivet nodes on Railway, on a control plane on another cloud.
- [Rivet Cloud](https://alchemy.run/rivet/rivet-cloud) — Use Rivet Cloud as the control plane, sign in to it from the alchemy CLI or CI, and run your nodes on Rivet Cloud or on any cloud.

## Effect Cluster

Effect Cluster entities, workflows, singletons and crons, on a Postgres database and a pool of runners you run on Docker, AWS, GCP, Kubernetes, Fly or Hetzner, or on Cloudflare Durable Objects, called by id from any runtime.

- [Effect Cluster](https://alchemy.run/cluster) — Run Effect Cluster entities, workflows, singletons and crons with Alchemy — a Postgres database and a pool of runners on Docker, AWS, GCP, Kubernetes, Fly or Hetzner, or Durable Objects on Cloudflare.
- [What is Effect Cluster?](https://alchemy.run/cluster/what-is-effect-cluster) — The concepts behind Effect Cluster — entities addressed by id, messages handled one at a time, shards, runners and pools, the database, workflows, singletons and crons — and how @alchemy.run/effect-cluster deploys them.
- [Setup](https://alchemy.run/cluster/setup) — Install the Effect Cluster provider and get Docker ready to run a cluster on your machine.
- [Part 1: Your First Entity](https://alchemy.run/cluster/tutorial/part-1) — Run an Effect Cluster database and runners on Docker, and deploy a chat room entity that tracks who's in it.
- [Part 2: Signed-In Members](https://alchemy.run/cluster/tutorial/part-2) — Add Effect RPC middleware so a room only lets signed-in users join, and provide it with the pool.
- [Part 3: Invitations](https://alchemy.run/cluster/tutorial/part-3) — Add a durable workflow that invites someone to a room, waits for their answer, and lets them in.
- [Part 4: Run It on AWS](https://alchemy.run/cluster/tutorial/part-4) — Move the chat rooms from Docker to AWS by swapping the database, the pool and the API's host.
- [Entities](https://alchemy.run/cluster/entities) — How an Effect Cluster entity is written in Alchemy — its declaration, its two-phase implementation, its instances, and where its code lives.
- [Calling an entity](https://alchemy.run/cluster/calling) — Call an Effect Cluster entity from any runtime by id — RPCs, streams, typed errors, fire-and-forget messages and headers.
- [RPC middleware](https://alchemy.run/cluster/middleware) — Authenticate and enrich every message to an entity with Effect RPC middleware — a server side that runs on the pool and a client side that runs in the caller.
- [Workflows](https://alchemy.run/cluster/workflows) — Durable workflows on Effect Cluster — persisted activities, durable sleeps, signals, compensations and child workflows — declared and implemented like an entity and started from any runtime.
- [Singletons](https://alchemy.run/cluster/singletons) — Run one fiber across the whole cluster with an Effect Cluster singleton — on exactly one runner, moved when that runner stops.
- [Crons](https://alchemy.run/cluster/crons) — Run a job on a schedule with an Effect Cluster cron — once per scheduled time across the cluster, with the schedule on its Layer.
- [Existing programs](https://alchemy.run/cluster/existing-programs) — Deploy an Effect Cluster program you already have, unchanged, on a pool of its own, and call its entities from any runtime.
- [Databases](https://alchemy.run/cluster/databases) — The Postgres an Effect Cluster coordinates through — what runners keep in it, and how to run one on any cloud or connect to one you have.
- [Pools](https://alchemy.run/cluster/pools) — How a pool of Effect Cluster runners hosts your entities, workflows, singletons and crons — what's bundled together, shard groups, the gateway, and how to split work across pools.
- [Docker](https://alchemy.run/cluster/docker) — Run an Effect Cluster's database and runners on a Docker swarm, on your machine or a server.
- [AWS](https://alchemy.run/cluster/aws) — Run an Effect Cluster's database on RDS and its runners on ECS Fargate, called from Lambda or anywhere through a load balancer.
- [GCP](https://alchemy.run/cluster/gcp) — Run an Effect Cluster's database and runners on Compute Engine, called from Cloud Run or anywhere through a regional load balancer.
- [Kubernetes](https://alchemy.run/cluster/kubernetes) — Run an Effect Cluster's database and runners on any Kubernetes cluster — EKS, GKE, or kind on your machine.
- [Fly](https://alchemy.run/cluster/fly) — Run an Effect Cluster's database and runners on Fly.io, on a private network, with the gateway at the pool's fly.dev address.
- [Hetzner](https://alchemy.run/cluster/hetzner) — Run an Effect Cluster's database and runners on Hetzner Cloud Servers, on a private Network, behind a Load Balancer.
- [Cloudflare](https://alchemy.run/cluster/cloudflare) — Run an Effect Cluster's entities, workflows, singletons and crons on Cloudflare Durable Objects, with no database and no servers to manage.

## Daytona

Daytona sandboxes from Workers and Lambda: what Daytona is, organizations and scoped API keys, snapshots (images, Dockerfile builds, warm bases), sandboxes and their lifecycle, programs in a sandbox, volumes, the toolbox, network limits and previews, secrets the sandbox can't read, regions and runners, and telemetry.

- [Daytona](https://alchemy.run/daytona) — Run code you don't fully trust in Daytona sandboxes. Declare snapshots, volumes and secrets in your Stack, and create, drive and delete sandboxes from any Worker or Lambda.
- [What is Daytona?](https://alchemy.run/daytona/what-is-daytona) — The concepts behind Daytona — organizations, API keys, regions and runners, snapshots, sandboxes and their lifecycle, the toolbox, previews, volumes, network limits and secrets — and how @alchemy.run/daytona models each of them.
- [Setup](https://alchemy.run/daytona/setup) — Sign Alchemy in to Daytona, or give it an API key.

## Daytona — Tutorial

- [Part 1: Build a Warm Snapshot](https://alchemy.run/daytona/tutorial/part-1) — Declare a Daytona snapshot of an image, and a warm snapshot of it with a repository cloned, both built at deploy time.
- [Part 2: Start Sandboxes from It](https://alchemy.run/daytona/tutorial/part-2) — A Cloudflare Worker that starts a fresh Daytona sandbox from the warm snapshot for each request.
- [Part 3: A Copy per User](https://alchemy.run/daytona/tutorial/part-3) — Give each user a Daytona sandbox started from the warm snapshot, which stops when idle and starts again with their changes.
- [Part 4: Update the Snapshot](https://alchemy.run/daytona/tutorial/part-4) — Move the Daytona snapshots to a new Node.js version, redeploy, and see new sandboxes start from it while existing ones keep theirs.
- [Part 5: Testing](https://alchemy.run/daytona/tutorial/part-5) — Deploy the Stack in a test, start sandboxes from the warm snapshot, and check what they contain.
- [Part 6: Stages and CI](https://alchemy.run/daytona/tutorial/part-6) — Deploy a stage per environment and per pull request, each with its own Daytona snapshots and Worker.

## Daytona — Accounts & access

- [Organizations and API keys](https://alchemy.run/daytona/organizations-and-keys) — How a Daytona organization holds your sandboxes and bill, how your profile picks the organization Alchemy deploys to, and the API key each Worker gets.
- [Members and roles](https://alchemy.run/daytona/organization/organization) — Give people access to a Daytona organization with roles, invitations and members, sign them in with single sign-on, and set organization defaults.
- [Secrets](https://alchemy.run/daytona/security/secrets) — Give a Daytona sandbox credentials it can use but not read, shared or one per user, with values from .env or a secrets manager.

## Daytona — Sandboxes

- [Programs in a sandbox](https://alchemy.run/daytona/sandboxes/programs) — Run an Effect program you write inside a Daytona sandbox, redeploy it without losing the sandbox, mount volumes into it, and install mount clients with a derived snapshot.
- [Regions and runners](https://alchemy.run/daytona/sandboxes/runners) — Where Daytona sandboxes run — shared regions, the region a sandbox picks, and a region of your own with runners on machines you operate.
- [Sandboxes](https://alchemy.run/daytona/sandboxes/sandboxes) — How a Daytona sandbox moves between started, stopped, archived and deleted, and how to create sandboxes per request or per user from a Worker, or declare a long-lived dev box in your Stack.
- [Snapshots](https://alchemy.run/daytona/sandboxes/snapshots) — Pull an image, build a Dockerfile on Daytona, or capture a warm base that sandboxes start from.
- [Toolbox](https://alchemy.run/daytona/sandboxes/toolbox) — Run commands, edit files, use git and language servers, open previews and SSH into a sandbox.
- [Volumes](https://alchemy.run/daytona/sandboxes/volumes) — Keep files in volumes that outlive sandboxes, shared or one per user.

## Daytona — Networking

## Git

A git server you build in one file, use like any remote, and reshape one block at a time: setup, a six-part tutorial (push, access control, publishing, per-user credentials, your app's API, branch protection), the REST and GitHub-compatible planes, the building blocks with their implementations, and recipes with the scaling model and measurements.

- [Git](https://alchemy.run/git) — A pluggable, embeddable, self-hostable git server on Cloudflare Workers, Durable Objects, and R2. Smart HTTP for any client, a typed REST plane with pull requests, and a GitHub-compatible API.
- [What is a git host?](https://alchemy.run/git/what-is-git) — The concepts behind hosting git — objects, refs, packs, the smart HTTP protocol, pushes and their verification, repositories, names and pull requests — and how @alchemy.run/git builds a host from them.
- [Getting Started](https://alchemy.run/git/getting-started) — A complete quickstart for a Git host protected by a shared credential. Deploy it to Cloudflare, push a repository, and clone it back.
- [Part 1: Push your first repository](https://alchemy.run/git/tutorial/part-1) — Deploy a Git host, push a commit, and clone it back. Add storage and hashing one layer at a time.
- [Part 2: Control access](https://alchemy.run/git/tutorial/part-2) — Protect the existing Git host with one shared credential, then verify both accepted and rejected requests.
- [Part 3: Publish a repository](https://alchemy.run/git/tutorial/part-3) — Allow anonymous clones of public repositories while preserving authenticated writes.
- [Part 4: Give users their own credentials](https://alchemy.run/git/tutorial/part-4) — Replace the shared credential with Better Auth accounts and individual Git API keys.
- [Part 5: Add your application's API](https://alchemy.run/git/tutorial/part-5) — Add a typed /me endpoint beside Git and use the caller already supplied by your authentication middleware.
- [Part 6: Protect a branch](https://alchemy.run/git/tutorial/part-6) — Authorize parsed Git mutations in ordinary HTTP handlers, using the request's user before committing changes.
- [Cloning & pushing](https://alchemy.run/git/clone-and-push) — Standard git clients over smart HTTP. What the wire supports, where credentials go, and what to do when something hangs.
- [Repositories](https://alchemy.run/git/repositories) — Create, fork, import, and manage repositories over the typed REST plane.
- [Pull requests](https://alchemy.run/git/pull-requests) — Server-side merge base, tree diffs, and fast-forward or three-way merges, computed inside the repository.
- [GitHub API compatibility](https://alchemy.run/git/github-api) — Point the gh CLI and Octokit at your host with the /api/v3 facade.
- [Overview](https://alchemy.run/git/blocks) — One layer graph, provided once, builds the Worker and every Durable Object behind it. Each line is a decision with implementations you choose or write.
- [HTTP routes](https://alchemy.run/git/blocks/server) — Compose Git route layers beside your application's Effect HTTP API, with your middleware and server.
- [Engine operations](https://alchemy.run/git/blocks/engine) — Build your own HTTP API over Git operations, with scoped preparation, application authorization, and explicit commit.
- [Repository](https://alchemy.run/git/blocks/repositories) — One Durable Object per repository, behind the Git.RepoStore service. Provide it, call it from your own routes, compose operations through Git.Engine, or implement its shape over another store.
- [Registry](https://alchemy.run/git/blocks/registry) — The registry resolves owner/name to a repository and serves listings. Keep it in a Durable Object or move it to a D1 database.
- [Blob Store](https://alchemy.run/git/blocks/blob-store) — Bulk, immutable, content-addressed bytes. R2 by default, S3 when data has to live in AWS, or any store that can do ranged reads and multipart writes.
- [Hasher](https://alchemy.run/git/blocks/hasher) — Every object a push sends is inflated and hashed before a ref moves. That is CPU, and where it runs is a Layer, in the Worker, in dynamically loaded Workers, or on Lambda.
- [Authentication and authorization](https://alchemy.run/git/blocks/auth) — Use native Effect HTTP middleware and ordinary application effects to authorize Git operations.
- [Overview](https://alchemy.run/git/recipes) — Requirements pick lines. One table from what you need to the line that changes, the stack shape for one cloud or two, and complete files to copy.
- [Scaling](https://alchemy.run/git/recipes/scaling) — Reads scale like a CDN and writes scale like git. The shape, the per-repository limits, the measured numbers, and a worked example of pushing something large and swapping the hasher.
- [All on Cloudflare](https://alchemy.run/git/recipes/cloudflare) — A git host on one Cloudflare account. One Worker, one bucket, two Durable Object namespaces, and dynamically loaded Workers hashing large pushes.
- [Bytes in S3, hashing on Lambda](https://alchemy.run/git/recipes/cloudflare-aws) — Compute on Cloudflare, bytes in S3, and large pushes hashed one Lambda per chunk. One stack carries both provider sets, and Alchemy mints the cross-cloud identity.
- [Bring your own store](https://alchemy.run/git/recipes/your-own-store) — Bytes have to live somewhere that is neither R2 nor S3. Implement the five operations of Git.BlobStore and provide it in place of the shipped Layers.

## Stripe

Products, prices, coupons, customers, payment links, and webhooks as Stack resources. HTTP bindings run inside a Worker or Lambda.

- [Stripe](https://alchemy.run/stripe) — Sell subscriptions and onboard merchants from a Cloudflare Worker — catalog, Checkout, the Billing Portal, Connect, and webhooks declared next to the code that uses them.
- [What is Stripe?](https://alchemy.run/stripe/what-is-stripe) — The concepts behind Stripe — accounts and test mode, API keys, products and prices, customers, Checkout, subscriptions, the Billing Portal, webhooks and Connect — and how @alchemy.run/stripe models each of them.
- [Accounts and API keys](https://alchemy.run/stripe/accounts-and-keys) — How a Stripe account and its test mode keep data apart, how secret and restricted keys differ, and which key Alchemy deploys with and which your runtimes hold.
- [Setup](https://alchemy.run/stripe/setup) — Connect alchemy to Stripe — secret key, profiles, CI, and how Worker bindings get their credentials.
- [Sell a subscription](https://alchemy.run/stripe/guides/subscriptions) — The full SaaS billing loop on one Cloudflare Worker — hosted Checkout, the Billing Portal, and webhooks that keep an entitlement record your app gates on.
- [Onboard merchants with Connect](https://alchemy.run/stripe/guides/connect) — Build a Connect platform on a Cloudflare Worker — create Express accounts, send merchants through hosted onboarding, and learn from account.updated when they can take payments.
- [React to Stripe events](https://alchemy.run/stripe/guides/webhooks) — consumeEvents provisions the webhook endpoint and runs one Effect per delivery. When to use it, which events to listen for, and how to manage the endpoint yourself.

## Docker

Local and CI Docker as Stack resources — images, containers, networks, and volumes driven through the active Docker CLI context; cloud container runtimes (Cloudflare Containers, ECS) consume the pushed image refs from their own hubs.

- [Docker](https://alchemy.run/docker) — Docker builds applications into images and runs them as isolated containers on a Docker engine, on your laptop, a CI runner or a server.
- [What is Docker?](https://alchemy.run/docker/what-is-docker) — The concepts behind Docker — engines and contexts, images and Dockerfiles, registries, containers, networks, volumes and Swarm — and how @alchemy.run/docker models each of them.
- [Setup](https://alchemy.run/docker/setup) — Install @alchemy.run/docker, register its providers, and point Alchemy at a Docker or Podman engine.
- [Engines & contexts](https://alchemy.run/docker/engines-and-contexts) — How a Docker context chooses the engine a resource lands on — the CLI's current context, a Docker.Context over SSH or TCP, an existing context by lookup — and who can reach an engine.
- [Registries & credentials](https://alchemy.run/docker/registries) — Give an image its registry credentials as a Redacted Config value, push without docker login, pull private base images, and read the password from a secrets manager per stage.
- [Build images](https://alchemy.run/docker/build-images) — Build an image from a Dockerfile with Docker.Image — build args, multi-stage targets, platforms, build secrets — and know when a deploy rebuilds it.
- [Build caches](https://alchemy.run/docker/build-caches) — Keep an image's build layers in a registry or GitHub Actions cache, so fresh CI runners skip the steps that didn't change.
- [Pull & mirror images](https://alchemy.run/docker/remote-images) — Pull an existing image with Docker.RemoteImage, pin it so deploys stop re-pulling, and re-tag and push it into your own registry.
- [Images on cloud runtimes](https://alchemy.run/docker/cloud-runtimes) — Hand a pushed image's reference or digest to ECS, Cloudflare Containers, Cloud Run or Kubernetes, let those runtimes build with your local Docker, and write Dockerfiles inline with Dockerfile.inline.
- [Containers](https://alchemy.run/docker/containers) — Run an image as a Docker.Container — start it, publish ports, pass secrets through its environment, health-check it, reach the host — and know which changes recreate it.
- [Networks](https://alchemy.run/docker/networks) — Connect containers on a Docker.Network so they reach each other by name, cut a network off from the internet, pin its subnet, and attach to networks you didn't create.
- [Volumes](https://alchemy.run/docker/volumes) — Keep a container's data in a Docker.Volume so it survives the container being recreated, mount host directories, and know when a volume and its data are deleted.
- [Limits & security](https://alchemy.run/docker/limits-and-security) — Cap a container's memory, CPU and processes, run it as an unprivileged user with a read-only filesystem and no capabilities, apply seccomp and AppArmor profiles, and rotate its logs.
- [Swarms](https://alchemy.run/docker/swarm) — Turn an engine into a swarm with Docker.Swarm, locally or on a server over SSH, use a swarm you didn't create, and grow it to more nodes.
- [Services](https://alchemy.run/docker/services) — Run replicated containers on a swarm with Docker.Service — publish ports through the routing mesh, roll out new images with automatic rollback, connect services on overlay networks, mount Swarm secrets, and place tasks on nodes.
- [Effectful services](https://alchemy.run/docker/effectful-services) — Write a Swarm service as an Effect program in your own code — Alchemy bundles it into an image on the swarm's engine, serves its fetch handler, runs its background loops and gives it the Config it reads.
- [Local Postgres](https://alchemy.run/docker/local-services) — Run Postgres for local development as Stack resources — a pinned image, a network and a volume, a Redacted password, and a health-checked container.

## Kubernetes

Cluster-agnostic Kubernetes workloads — Deployments, Jobs and CronJobs (as images or Effect programs), raw manifests, and Helm charts — on a local cluster or any cluster reachable through a kubeconfig, token, client certificate, or exec plugin.

- [Kubernetes](https://alchemy.run/kubernetes) — Run containers and Effect programs on any Kubernetes cluster with Alchemy. Declare Deployments, Jobs, raw manifests, and Helm charts in the same typed program as the rest of your infrastructure. No YAML, no kubectl apply.
- [What is Kubernetes?](https://alchemy.run/kubernetes/what-is-kubernetes) — The concepts behind Kubernetes — clusters, nodes, the API server, namespaces, Pods, Deployments, Services, Jobs, ConfigMaps and Secrets, images, manifests, server-side apply and Helm — and how @alchemy.run/kubernetes models each of them.
- [Setup](https://alchemy.run/kubernetes/setup) — Install Alchemy and connect it to a Kubernetes cluster, whether a local cluster on your machine, any cluster in your kubeconfig, or an explicit connection for CI. Then add a registry for images built from your code.
- [Part 1: Your First Deployment](https://alchemy.run/kubernetes/tutorial/part-1) — Create a Stack, start a Kubernetes cluster on your machine with Kubernetes.LocalCluster, deploy a replicated HTTP service with Kubernetes.Deployment, and reach it with kubectl.
- [Part 2: Namespaces & Configuration](https://alchemy.run/kubernetes/tutorial/part-2) — Create a Namespace with Kubernetes.Manifest, move the Deployment into it, and configure the app with environment variables and resource limits.
- [Part 3: Effect Jobs](https://alchemy.run/kubernetes/tutorial/part-3) — Write a smoke test as an Effect program, run it as a Kubernetes Job that Alchemy builds and pushes for you, watch it re-run when the program changes, and schedule it as a CronJob.
- [Part 4: Install a Helm Chart](https://alchemy.run/kubernetes/tutorial/part-4) — Install metrics-server from its Helm chart with Kubernetes.HelmChart, pass chart values, and check pod metrics with kubectl top.
- [Part 5: Deploy to Your Own Cluster](https://alchemy.run/kubernetes/tutorial/part-5) — Point the tutorial stack at a hosted Kubernetes cluster such as GKE, AKS, EKS, k3s, or anything in your kubeconfig. Keep the local cluster for development with stages, and clean up.
- [Connecting to clusters](https://alchemy.run/kubernetes/clusters/connecting) — Point Kubernetes resources at any cluster with Kubernetes.KubeConfig, a raw Kubernetes.Connection (bearer token, client certificate, or exec plugin), or a cluster resource such as Kubernetes.LocalCluster.
- [Container registries](https://alchemy.run/kubernetes/clusters/registries) — Give a Kubernetes connection a registry so Deployments and Jobs built from Effect programs or Dockerfiles are pushed where the cluster's nodes can pull them, such as GHCR, Docker Hub, Artifact Registry, ACR, or a registry of your own.
- [Local clusters](https://alchemy.run/kubernetes/clusters/local) — Run a Kubernetes cluster on your machine with Kubernetes.LocalCluster. It is a kind cluster in Docker with an image registry wired into its nodes, so Effect programs and Dockerfiles deploy the same way they do on a hosted cluster.
- [Amazon EKS](https://alchemy.run/kubernetes/clusters/eks) — Run Alchemy's Kubernetes resources on Amazon EKS. Find the guide for creating clusters, ECR images, Pod Identity, and load balancers.
- [Cluster adapters](https://alchemy.run/kubernetes/clusters/cluster-adapters) — The extension point between Alchemy's cluster-agnostic Kubernetes resources and the platform a cluster runs on. Covers authentication, image registries, workload identity, load balancer defaults, and how to write your own.
- [Deployments](https://alchemy.run/kubernetes/workloads/deployments) — Run a replicated server on any Kubernetes cluster with Kubernetes.Deployment. Covers names, namespaces, Service types and URLs, replicas, resources, labels, the pod template escape hatch, and Effect servers.
- [Jobs & CronJobs](https://alchemy.run/kubernetes/workloads/jobs) — Run work to completion with Kubernetes.Job, as a container image or as an Effect program, and on a schedule as a CronJob. Covers how Job names, re-runs, retries, and cleanup work.
- [Container images](https://alchemy.run/kubernetes/workloads/images) — Choose where a Deployment or Job's container image comes from and where built images are pushed. Sources are a registry reference, your own Dockerfile, or a bundled Effect program.
- [Configuration & bindings](https://alchemy.run/kubernetes/workloads/bindings) — Pass configuration into Kubernetes workloads with env and Outputs, understand the variables Alchemy sets, keep secrets out of plain text, and use bindings.
- [How objects are managed](https://alchemy.run/kubernetes/workloads/object-lifecycle) — How Alchemy applies, orders, prunes, and deletes Kubernetes objects, including server-side apply and field ownership, drift, replacement, unreachable clusters, and adoption.
- [Manifests](https://alchemy.run/kubernetes/objects/manifests) — Apply any single Kubernetes object with Kubernetes.Manifest, including Namespaces, ConfigMaps, Secrets, StatefulSets, Ingresses, CRDs and custom resources, and order objects with Output references.
- [Helm charts](https://alchemy.run/kubernetes/objects/helm-charts) — Install Helm charts with Kubernetes.HelmChart. Covers repository, OCI, and local charts, values, release names, namespaces, CRDs, hooks, and how Alchemy owns the rendered objects instead of a Helm release.

## SQL

Database comparison, Effect SQL, Drizzle, Prisma ORM v8 (Postgres-only), committed migrations, and connection lifecycle. Deployment walkthroughs live with their runtime providers.

- [SQL](https://alchemy.run/sql) — Choose a database, connect with Effect SQL, Drizzle, or Prisma ORM, and deploy committed migrations.
- [How SQL works in Alchemy](https://alchemy.run/sql/what-is-sql) — The concepts behind SQL in Alchemy — databases and engines, clients, connections and pools, request scope, migrations and their history — and how they fit together on every cloud.
- [Databases](https://alchemy.run/sql/databases) — Compare database engines, connection paths, and deployment guides across Alchemy's SQL providers.
- [Postgres](https://alchemy.run/sql/effect-sql/postgres) — SQL.Postgres turns a connection string into an @effect/sql-pg client — tagged-template queries with typed errors, one pool per execution.
- [MySQL](https://alchemy.run/sql/effect-sql/mysql) — SQL.MySQL turns a connection string into an @effect/sql-mysql2 client — portable tagged-template queries with typed errors and one pool per execution.
- [D1](https://alchemy.run/sql/effect-sql/d1) — SQL.D1 wraps a bound D1 database in an @effect/sql-d1 client — tagged-template queries with typed errors over the native binding.
- [libSQL](https://alchemy.run/sql/effect-sql/libsql) — Run SQL on a libSQL database, such as Turso, with Effect SQL.
- [Migrations](https://alchemy.run/sql/effect-sql/migrations) — Commit ordered SQL files and apply them on database deploy or Durable Object activation, tracked in one Alchemy-owned table.
- [Connection lifecycle](https://alchemy.run/sql/effect-sql/lifecycle) — SQL and Drizzle clients build lazily, reuse a client within the current execution scope, and release resources when that scope closes.
- [Postgres](https://alchemy.run/sql/drizzle/postgres) — Provider-neutral Postgres schemas, Effect-native Drizzle queries, and connections for Workers, Lambda, and servers.
- [MySQL](https://alchemy.run/sql/drizzle/mysql) — Provider-neutral MySQL schemas, Effect-native Drizzle queries, and connection configuration.
- [D1](https://alchemy.run/sql/drizzle/d1) — SQLite schemas and Effect-native Drizzle queries over a Cloudflare D1 binding.
- [libSQL](https://alchemy.run/sql/drizzle/libsql) — Use Drizzle with a libSQL database, such as Turso.
- [Migrations](https://alchemy.run/sql/drizzle/migrations) — Generate migrations when your schema changes, review and commit the SQL and snapshots, then deploy from Git.
- [Postgres](https://alchemy.run/sql/prisma/postgres) — Connect Prisma ORM v8 to Postgres and run Effect-native queries, streams, prepared statements, and transactions independently of your cloud provider.
- [Contracts](https://alchemy.run/sql/prisma/contracts) — Author Prisma ORM v8 contracts in Prisma Schema Language or TypeScript, generate optional Effect bindings and row schemas, and connect them to migrations.
- [Migrations](https://alchemy.run/sql/prisma/migrations) — How Prisma.Contract and Prisma.Migrate run Prisma's contract emission, migration planning, and graph-ordered apply inside alchemy deploy.

## Command

Cloud-agnostic local process primitives — memoized builds, one-off commands, and dev servers; the static-site guides in each cloud hub consume them under the hood.

- [Command](https://alchemy.run/command) — Alchemy's cloud-agnostic primitives for local processes in the deploy graph — memoized builds, one-off commands, and dev servers.
- [How commands work](https://alchemy.run/command/what-is-command) — How Command puts local processes into a Stack — builds that produce assets, one-off commands run for their effects, dev servers — and how memoization decides when each runs again.
- [Memoization: builds & one-off commands](https://alchemy.run/command/memoization) — Content-hash memoization shared by Command.Build and Command.Exec — what gets hashed, when a command re-runs, and the outdir contract on destroy.
- [Dev servers](https://alchemy.run/command/dev-servers) — Run a framework dev server as a Command.Dev resource — started by alchemy dev, a no-op on alchemy deploy, with the server's URL surfaced back into your stack.

## ACME

TLS certificates from any ACME certificate authority as Stack resources, validated over DNS, renewed on deploy, or issued at runtime.

- [ACME](https://alchemy.run/acme) — Manage TLS certificates independently of your hosting provider, at deploy time or from an application.
- [What is ACME?](https://alchemy.run/acme/what-is-acme) — The concepts behind ACME certificates — certificate authorities, accounts, orders, challenges and DNS-01 validation, certificates and keys, renewal and revocation — and how @alchemy.run/acme models each of them.
- [Getting started](https://alchemy.run/acme/getting-started) — Issue a staging TLS certificate with Let's Encrypt and an existing Cloudflare DNS zone.
- [Certificate authorities](https://alchemy.run/acme/certificate-authorities) — Select a CA, configure external account binding, and understand account identity and key storage.
- [DNS validation](https://alchemy.run/acme/dns-validation) — Configure Cloudflare DNS-01 challenges, wildcard certificates, propagation, and custom solvers.
- [Renewal & revocation](https://alchemy.run/acme/renewal) — Schedule renewal, understand replacement and deletion, and protect certificate and account keys.
- [Runtime issuance](https://alchemy.run/acme/runtime) — Deploy an authenticated Worker that issues and revokes certificates using a bound ACME account.
- [Using certificates](https://alchemy.run/acme/using-certificates) — Upload an ACME certificate to Fly or pass its chain and private key to another TLS consumer.
- [Troubleshooting](https://alchemy.run/acme/troubleshooting) — Diagnose failed DNS challenges, rejected orders, rate limits, and runtime certificate operations.

## Domain

A domain-driven design framework: model commands, events, aggregates, views, projections, policies, and sagas once, then host them on Cloudflare, Rivet, Effect Cluster or in memory.

- [Domain](https://alchemy.run/domain) — A domain-driven design framework for Effect. Model your business as commands, aggregates, events, views, projections and policies, test it in memory, and run it on Durable Objects on Cloudflare, Rivet or Effect Cluster.
- [What is Domain-Driven Design?](https://alchemy.run/domain/what-is-ddd) — The concepts of Domain-Driven Design, event sourcing and CQRS, and how they fit together to model a business.
- [Project layout](https://alchemy.run/domain/project-layout) — How to lay out an @alchemy.run/domain project. One file per building block, named after its noun and its kind; folders per subdomain; a pure domain package, a server package that hosts it, and a foldkit web package, wired in one stack.
- [Part 1: Model an account](https://alchemy.run/domain/tutorial/part-1) — Declare events, commands and rejections, decide them in an aggregate, and check it with stories.
- [Part 2: Read it with a view](https://alchemy.run/domain/tutorial/part-2) — Show each account's balance and a statement of every movement, kept up to date as events arrive.
- [Part 3: React with a policy](https://alchemy.run/domain/tutorial/part-3) — Register customers, and open a main account for each one with a policy.
- [Part 4: Expose an Api](https://alchemy.run/domain/tutorial/part-4) — Authenticate requests, let customers act only on their own accounts, and expose the bank through a typed Api.
- [Part 5: Deploy to Cloudflare](https://alchemy.run/domain/tutorial/part-5) — Host the bank on Durable Objects behind a Worker, run it locally, deploy it, and watch a balance change live.
- [Part 6: Build the UI with foldkit](https://alchemy.run/domain/tutorial/part-6) — A browser app that signs in with a cookie, opens an account, deposits, and watches its balance live.
- [Part 7: Observe it](https://alchemy.run/domain/tutorial/part-7) — Send the bank's traces and logs to Axiom, follow a deposit through every Durable Object it reaches, and trace clicks from the browser.
- [Part 8: Change a deployed model](https://alchemy.run/domain/tutorial/part-8) — Change what a view computes after it has data, add a view over every account, and follow what each deploy does with the events already recorded.
- [Domain Model](https://alchemy.run/domain/model) — What a domain model contains, how it processes every command, and how you declare, run and use one.
- [Command](https://alchemy.run/domain/command) — How a command names its target, carries its data, declares every outcome, and reaches its aggregate exactly once.
- [Event](https://alchemy.run/domain/event) — What an event records, what to put in it, how it's stored, and how the rest of the model consumes it.
- [Aggregate](https://alchemy.run/domain/aggregate) — How an aggregate holds state, decides commands, applies events, and keeps its rules consistent.
- [View](https://alchemy.run/domain/view) — How a view folds events into a read model per key, emits events of its own, combines other views, and serves reads.
- [Projection](https://alchemy.run/domain/projection) — How a projection consumes events into a store you own, in order per key, batched and replayable, and why it never sends commands.
- [Stream](https://alchemy.run/domain/stream) — How a stream keeps a keyed, append-only log that a projection writes and clients read through an Api, with its latest entry as the current value.
- [Query](https://alchemy.run/domain/query) — How a query serves a projection's store to clients across keys, typed, authorized by its handler, paged by cursor, and consistent with the caller's own writes.
- [Policy](https://alchemy.run/domain/policy) — How a policy reacts to events with commands and calls to outside systems, and how to make it safe to run more than once.
- [Saga](https://alchemy.run/domain/saga) — A process that spans several aggregates and takes time, run step by step as an Effect workflow, with steps that undo earlier ones when a later one fails.
- [External System](https://alchemy.run/domain/external-system) — Declare the outside systems your model calls in the model's own language, implement them with Layers, and turn their events into commands.
- [Api](https://alchemy.run/domain/api) — How an Api publishes a model to one kind of client, how it's served, and how a typed client calls it.
- [Annotations](https://alchemy.run/domain/annotations) — Describe every declaration in an @alchemy.run/domain model, show the descriptions in MCP tools, CLI help and OpenAPI, and add keys of your own for tooling built on the model.
- [Cloudflare Durable Objects](https://alchemy.run/domain/cloudflare) — Host a domain model on Durable Objects behind a Worker, with live reads over WebSockets.
- [Rivet](https://alchemy.run/domain/rivet) — Host a domain model on Rivet Durable Objects, on nodes in any cloud, and serve its Apis from any runtime.
- [Effect Cluster](https://alchemy.run/domain/effect-cluster) — Host a domain model on Effect Cluster entities, with its state in Postgres and its runners on any cloud.
- [In memory](https://alchemy.run/domain/in-memory) — Run a domain model in a single process, for tests and for apps that don't need Cloudflare.
- [Story](https://alchemy.run/domain/story) — A specification you can run. Given some history, when a command is sent, then these events are recorded.
- [Testing a model](https://alchemy.run/domain/testing-models) — Test your model's rules, views, policies and deadlines with stories that run it in memory.
- [Testing an Api](https://alchemy.run/domain/testing-apis) — Test what each client may do and see, in process, over HTTP, and against a real deployment.
- [Plain HTTP and OpenAPI](https://alchemy.run/domain/http-api) — Publish an Api as a plain HTTP JSON API, with an OpenAPI document, from the same Api.
- [CLI](https://alchemy.run/domain/cli) — Run an Api's calls from a terminal, as a person or an agent, against the deployed Api.
- [MCP](https://alchemy.run/domain/mcp) — Give an agent the commands and reads of an Api as tools, inside the app with Effect AI, or outside it over MCP.
- [Integrate with Foldkit](https://alchemy.run/domain/foldkit) — Derive Foldkit Commands from an Api, ask its queries, follow View snapshots, and seed the Model from Flags.
- [Optimistic updates](https://alchemy.run/domain/optimistic-updates) — Show pending intent, confirm it by commandId from a View feed, and retry an unknown outcome safely.
- [Offline and local first](https://alchemy.run/domain/local-first) — Choose how local an app is, and keep it working offline by recording intents and sending them when the connection returns.
- [Sessions and middleware](https://alchemy.run/domain/sessions) — Authenticate every request, carry who is asking into the domain, and sign browsers in with a cookie.
- [Sign in with better-auth](https://alchemy.run/domain/better-auth) — Sign users in to a Domain Api with GitHub or Google through better-auth, and give every command and view the signed-in user.
- [Views as security boundaries](https://alchemy.run/domain/view-security) — Decide who may read each view, keep watches honest as data changes hands, and give each audience a view of its own.
- [Unique values](https://alchemy.run/domain/unique-values) — Keep a value unique across every customer by making the value itself an aggregate.
- [Deadlines](https://alchemy.run/domain/deadlines) — Give a waiting process a time limit with a scheduled command, and let the aggregate decide whether the deadline or the action wins.
- [History at scale](https://alchemy.run/domain/backfill) — How a deploy backfills new views and projections on Cloudflare, how long it takes, and how to run a large Domain within Cloudflare's limits.
- [Observability](https://alchemy.run/domain/observability) — Trace how commands, events and reactions flow through an @alchemy.run/domain model, across Durable Objects and over hours. Automatic spans, correlation ids and metrics, plus the attributes your handlers record.

## API reference

Service-level API reference, generated from JSDoc on the source `.ts` files via `bun scripts/generate-api-reference.ts`. Each page groups resources and capabilities by service, with a heading per resource and examples extracted from source JSDoc.

The service-level pages are indexed in [llms-full.txt](https://alchemy.run/llms-full.txt), which repeats this entire file plus one link per service. Warning: it is large (~256 KB) — only fetch it when you need to locate a specific resource's reference page.
